sec01-F01-card.front: What credential must you hold before driving a car or truck on New Mexico public roads?
sec01-F01-card.expected_back: A person driving a motor vehicle on a New Mexico public road needs a driver license.

sec01-F02-card.front: Which state's driver license must a New Mexico resident hold?
sec01-F02-card.expected_back: A driver who resides in New Mexico must hold a New Mexico driver license.

sec01-F03-card.front: Which applicants follow New Mexico's graduated licensing system before earning an unrestricted license?
sec01-F03-card.expected_back: Applicants younger than eighteen use the graduated licensing system until they qualify for an unrestricted license.

sec01-F04-card.front: In what order do the three stages of New Mexico's graduated licensing system progress?
sec01-F04-card.expected_back: The graduated system progresses through an instructional permit, a provisional license and an unrestricted license.

sec01-F05-card.front: What minimum age and license class must a supervisor have when riding with an instructional-permit holder?
sec01-F05-card.expected_back: An instructional permit allows driving with supervision by someone aged at least twenty-one who holds a license for that type of vehicle.

sec01-F06-card.front: Where inside a passenger car must the supervising driver sit while a permit holder drives?
sec01-F06-card.expected_back: For a passenger car driven on an instructional permit, the supervising driver occupies the front passenger seat.

sec01-F07-card.front: At what minimum age can a New Mexico teen apply for an instructional permit?
sec01-F07-card.expected_back: Eligibility for an instructional permit begins at age fifteen.

sec01-F08-card.front: Which two screenings must an applicant pass to get an instructional permit?
sec01-F08-card.expected_back: An instructional permit applicant must pass both the knowledge examination and the vision examination.

sec01-F09-card.front: Whose signature is required on the consent form when an applicant is under eighteen?
sec01-F09-card.expected_back: An applicant younger than eighteen needs a parent or guardian to sign the consent form.

sec01-F10-card.front: What is the minimum length of time you must hold an instructional permit?
sec01-F10-card.expected_back: The instructional permit must be held for a minimum of six months.

sec01-F11-card.front: What driver-education course requirement applies to instructional-permit applicants aged fifteen and up?
sec01-F11-card.expected_back: For an instructional permit, an applicant aged at least fifteen must enroll in and attend driver education approved by the Traffic Safety Bureau, covering DWI and practice driving.

sec01-F12-card.front: How may an approved driving instructor supervise someone driving on an instructional permit?
sec01-F12-card.expected_back: Instructional-permit driving may be supervised by an approved instructor seated beside the learner.

sec01-F13-card.front: When no approved instructor sits beside a permit learner, what age and licensing history must the supervisor have?
sec01-F13-card.expected_back: For instructional-permit driving without an approved instructor beside the learner, the supervising licensed driver must be at least twenty-one and have held a license in New Mexico or another state for at least three years.

sec01-F14-card.front: Without a licensed adult twenty-one or older aboard, how many young non-family passengers may a provisional driver carry?
sec01-F14-card.expected_back: Without a licensed driver aged at least twenty-one in the vehicle, a provisional driver may carry no more than one passenger younger than twenty-one from outside the driver’s immediate family.

sec01-F15-card.front: At least how many behind-the-wheel practice hours are required before applying for a provisional license?
sec01-F15-card.expected_back: A provisional-license applicant needs at least fifty hours of practice behind the wheel.

sec01-F16-card.front: How many of the fifty required provisional practice hours must take place at night?
sec01-F16-card.expected_back: At least ten of the required practice hours for a provisional license must occur at night.

sec01-F17-card.front: Who must certify that a provisional-license applicant completed all required practice driving?
sec01-F17-card.expected_back: A provisional-license applicant’s parent or guardian must certify completion of the required driving practice.

sec01-F18-card.front: Which three evaluations must an applicant pass to earn a provisional license?
sec01-F18-card.expected_back: To receive a provisional license, the applicant must pass written and road examinations as well as vision screening.

sec01-F19-card.front: What minimum age and permit-holding time are required for a New Mexico provisional license?
sec01-F19-card.expected_back: For a provisional license, the minimum age is fifteen years and six months, and the applicant must have held an instructional permit for six months.

sec01-F20-card.front: How long before applying for a provisional license must your record stay free of traffic convictions?
sec01-F20-card.expected_back: A provisional applicant must have no traffic-violation conviction in the preceding ninety days.

sec01-F21-card.front: How long must you hold a provisional license right before upgrading to an unrestricted license?
sec01-F21-card.expected_back: An unrestricted-license applicant must have held a provisional license throughout the immediately preceding twelve months.

sec01-F22-card.front: What recent traffic-conviction rule applies when stepping up to an unrestricted license?
sec01-F22-card.expected_back: A person applying for an unrestricted license must have no traffic-violation conviction during the previous ninety days.

sec01-F23-card.front: How do unresolved, pending traffic citations affect an unrestricted-license application?
sec01-F23-card.expected_back: An unrestricted-license applicant must have no pending traffic violations.

sec01-F24-card.front: What alcohol- or drug-offense history during the provisional period disqualifies an unrestricted-license upgrade?
sec01-F24-card.expected_back: During the provisional period, an unrestricted-license applicant must have neither a guilty adjudication for an alcohol- or drug-use offense nor a pending offense involving that use.

sec01-R01-card.front: During which overnight hours does a provisional license normally bar driving on public highways?
sec01-R01-card.expected_back: A provisional license normally bars public-highway driving from midnight until five in the morning.

sec01-R02-card.front: Who riding inside the car lifts the provisional midnight-to-five curfew?
sec01-R02-card.expected_back: The provisional nighttime restriction does not apply when a licensed driver aged twenty-one or older accompanies the driver.

sec01-R03-card.front: What paperwork allows a provisional driver on the road after midnight for family necessity?
sec01-R03-card.expected_back: Family necessity is a permitted reason for provisional nighttime driving when supported by a parent’s or guardian’s signed statement.

sec01-R04-card.front: What written proof backs provisional nighttime driving for non-emergency medical necessity?
sec01-R04-card.expected_back: Medical necessity permits provisional nighttime driving when a parent or guardian provides a signed statement.

sec01-R05-card.front: Whose signed statement authorizes a provisional driver to commute between midnight and five for work?
sec01-R05-card.expected_back: Driving to or from work is a provisional nighttime exception when the driver’s employer provides a signed statement.

sec01-R06-card.front: Which four adults can sign a statement excusing provisional night travel for school or religious events?
sec01-R06-card.expected_back: Travel to or from school or a religious activity is a provisional nighttime exception with a signed statement from a school official, religious official, parent or guardian.

sec01-R07-card.front: Which urgent health situation excuses provisional driving between midnight and five?
sec01-R07-card.expected_back: A medical emergency is another exception to the provisional nighttime driving restriction.

sec01-R08-card.front: Which two validity lengths does the New Mexico handbook list for driver licenses?
sec01-R08-card.expected_back: The handbook describes driver licenses as having either four-year or eight-year validity.

sec01-R09-card.front: When does the handbook's license-renewal window open and close around expiration?
sec01-R09-card.expected_back: The renewal window described in the handbook begins ninety days before expiration and ends thirty days afterward.

sec01-R10-card.front: Which two items does the handbook instruct you to bring when renewing your license?
sec01-R10-card.expected_back: For renewal, the handbook directs a driver to bring the existing license and another identity document.

sec01-R11-card.front: Which evaluations can MVD require when you renew a driver license?
sec01-R11-card.expected_back: Renewal can require vision or knowledge testing and, in special cases, a driving examination.

sec01-R12-card.front: What happens to your driving privileges if you are convicted of driving impaired by alcohol or drugs?
sec01-R12-card.expected_back: A conviction for driving while impaired by alcohol or drugs can result in loss of driving privileges.

sec01-R13-card.front: How does refusing a police-requested alcohol or drug check affect your ability to drive?
sec01-R13-card.expected_back: Refusing an alcohol or drug test requested by a police officer can cost a driver the privilege to drive.

sec01-R14-card.front: What license consequence can follow leaving an involved crash without identifying yourself?
sec01-R14-card.expected_back: Leaving a crash in which you are involved without identifying yourself can result in loss of driving privileges.

sec01-R15-card.front: What can happen to your license if you put false information on a driver-license application?
sec01-R15-card.expected_back: False information on a driver-license application can lead to loss of driving privileges.

sec01-R16-card.front: How can failing to settle a court judgment for motor-vehicle crash damages affect you?
sec01-R16-card.expected_back: Failing to settle a judgment against you for motor-vehicle-crash damages can put your driving privileges at risk.

sec01-R17-card.front: How do altering your license or using someone else's card to buy alcohol affect your driving status?
sec01-R17-card.expected_back: Attempting to alter your license information or using another person’s license when trying to buy alcohol can lead to loss of driving privileges.

sec01-R18-card.front: What happens if MVD orders a driver reexamination and you fail to show up?
sec01-R18-card.expected_back: Failing to attend a reexamination requested by MVD can jeopardize the driver license.

sec01-R19-card.front: What privilege penalty applies to using a vehicle in a felony or causing a fatal crash?
sec01-R19-card.expected_back: Using a vehicle for a felony or causing a death in a vehicle crash can result in loss of driving privileges.

sec01-R20-card.front: What happens when too many violation points stack up on your driving record?
sec01-R20-card.expected_back: Accumulating excessive driving-record points can lead to loss of driving privileges.

sec01-R21-card.front: What risk do you run if you let another person use your driver license?
sec01-R21-card.expected_back: Allowing another person to use your driver license can lead to loss of driving privileges.

sec01-R22-card.front: What restraint check must happen before putting the vehicle in motion?
sec01-R22-card.expected_back: Before driving, buckle your belt and check that every passenger uses a belt or a child restraint.

sec01-R23-card.front: What should you do with the vehicle doors before setting off?
sec01-R23-card.expected_back: The handbook directs drivers to lock the vehicle doors before setting off.

sec01-R24-card.front: How does wearing a safety belt change crash outcomes?
sec01-R24-card.expected_back: Using a safety belt reduces the chance of death or injury in a crash.

sec01-R25-card.front: How does New Mexico law treat driving without wearing a safety belt?
sec01-R25-card.expected_back: The handbook states that driving without a safety belt violates New Mexico law.

sec01-R26-card.front: How must a two-part safety belt be worn to deliver full crash protection?
sec01-R26-card.expected_back: A two-part belt system provides its intended protection when both its lap portion and its shoulder portion are worn.

sec01-R27-card.front: What manual step is still mandatory in an older car with motorized automatic shoulder belts?
sec01-R27-card.expected_back: An automatic shoulder belt still requires fastening the separate lap belt.

sec01-R28-card.front: Up to what child age does the New Mexico handbook require appropriate restraints whenever moving?
sec01-R28-card.expected_back: The staged handbook says children younger than twelve must use appropriate restraints whenever the vehicle moves.

sec01-R29-card.front: Which age or weight thresholds require an approved child safety device in the handbook?
sec01-R29-card.memory_hook: Under twenty-four months or sixty pounds
sec01-R29-card.expected_back: The staged handbook says a child younger than twenty-four months or lighter than sixty pounds must use an approved safety device.

sec01-R30-card.front: Where inside the vehicle does the handbook recommend securing children?
sec01-R30-card.expected_back: The handbook recommends securing children in the rear seat.

sec01-R31-card.front: Where does the handbook warn caregivers never to secure a child, and why is it extra dangerous?
sec01-R31-card.expected_back: The handbook directs caregivers never to secure a child in the front passenger seat, especially when that position has an air bag.

sec01-R32-card.front: What option may help a caregiver who cannot afford an approved child safety seat?
sec01-R32-card.expected_back: Organizations may lend a child safety device to a caregiver who cannot afford one.

sec02-F01-card.front: Which three roadway features make up standard forms of traffic control?
sec02-F01-card.expected_back: Traffic signals, roadside signs and pavement markings are forms of traffic control.

sec02-F02-card.front: Which three authorized groups must you obey when they direct traffic in person?
sec02-F02-card.expected_back: Drivers must follow traffic directions given by law enforcement personnel, highway workers or school crossing guards.

sec02-F03-card.front: Under what condition does a green traffic light allow you to proceed?
sec02-F03-card.expected_back: A green traffic light allows travel only when proceeding is safe.

sec02-F04-card.front: How are red, yellow, and green positioned on a standard vertical traffic light?
sec02-F04-card.memory_hook: Red top, yellow middle, green bottom
sec02-F04-card.expected_back: In the usual vertical traffic signal, green is below yellow and red is above yellow.

sec02-F05-card.front: What legal duty stays active even as you enter an intersection on a steady green light?
sec02-F05-card.expected_back: A steady green light allows entry into the intersection while required yielding duties still apply.

sec02-F06-card.front: Before rolling forward when your red light turns green, what must happen inside the intersection?
sec02-F06-card.expected_back: When a stopped driver receives a green light, traffic already crossing must clear before the driver moves.

sec02-F07-card.front: What movement does a lighted green arrow authorize?
sec02-F07-card.expected_back: A green arrow authorizes a turn in its indicated direction.

sec02-F08-card.front: Who holds priority when you want to turn left on a circular steady green light?
sec02-F08-card.expected_back: A left turn on a steady green light is permitted only when safe, with oncoming traffic having priority.

sec02-F09-card.front: What should you scan for on posts or mast arms before turning left on a green light?
sec02-F09-card.expected_back: Before turning left on green, check for signs that forbid the turn.

sec02-F10-card.front: Who must you watch for across your path during both right turns and left turns?
sec02-F10-card.expected_back: During either a right turn or a left turn, watch for pedestrians crossing your path.

sec02-F11-card.front: What does a steady yellow traffic light warn of, and what action does it require?
sec02-F11-card.expected_back: A steady yellow light warns of the coming red light and requires stopping when stopping is safe.

sec02-F12-card.front: What should you do if the signal switches to yellow after you are already inside the intersection?
sec02-F12-card.expected_back: A driver already inside the intersection when yellow appears should continue through instead of stopping there.

sec02-F13-card.front: How must you adjust your driving at a flashing yellow traffic light?
sec02-F13-card.expected_back: A flashing yellow light calls for reduced speed and cautious travel.

sec02-F14-card.front: What phase is ending when a yellow arrow lights up, and how must a turning driver respond?
sec02-F14-card.expected_back: A yellow arrow ends protected turning time; if turning in its direction, prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

sec02-F15-card.front: What action is mandatory at a steady circular red traffic light?
sec02-F15-card.expected_back: A steady red light requires a stop.

sec02-F16-card.front: What does a bright blinking strobe inside a steady red lens mean?
sec02-F16-card.expected_back: A bright blinking light located inside a red signal is an added warning that the red light requires stopping.

sec02-R01-card.front: After halting for a red light, when may you drive straight ahead?
sec02-R01-card.expected_back: To travel straight after stopping at red, wait for green and for crossing traffic to clear.

sec02-R02-card.front: Which three conditions must all be met before turning right on a steady red light?
sec02-R02-card.expected_back: A right turn at red is allowed only after a complete stop, when safe, and when no sign forbids it.

sec02-R03-card.front: While preparing a permitted right turn on red, whom must you watch for directly ahead?
sec02-R03-card.expected_back: A driver making a permitted right turn at red must watch for pedestrians in front of the vehicle.

sec02-R04-card.front: Which roadside control matches the exact rule of a flashing red traffic signal?
sec02-R04-card.expected_back: A flashing red signal requires the same complete stop as a stop sign, followed by travel only when safe.

sec02-R05-card.front: What two commands does a steady red arrow enforce while illuminated?
sec02-R05-card.expected_back: A red arrow requires stopping and forbids movement in its direction while it remains red.

sec02-R06-card.front: What change at the signal head allows you to move after waiting at a red arrow?
sec02-R06-card.expected_back: Movement following a red arrow may begin after it goes out and a green arrow or green light appears.

sec04-F01-card.front: Besides separating traffic lanes, what three movements do pavement lines and symbols regulate?
sec04-F01-card.expected_back: Pavement lines and symbols separate traffic lanes and indicate permitted passing, lane changes and turning use.

sec04-F02-card.front: What two critical intersection zones can pavement markings designate for drivers and walkers?
sec04-F02-card.expected_back: Pavement markings can designate pedestrian crossings and the stopping position for a sign or signal.

sec04-F03-card.front: What does a continuous line painted along the side of a roadway identify?
sec04-F03-card.expected_back: A continuous line beside the roadway identifies its edge.

sec04-F04-card.front: What is true about the direction of traffic on both sides of white lane lines?
sec04-F04-card.expected_back: White lane lines separate streams of traffic moving the same way.

sec04-F05-card.front: When does a broken white lane line permit you to move into the next lane?
sec04-F05-card.expected_back: A broken white lane line allows a lane change after checking that the movement is safe.

sec04-F06-card.front: What does a solid white lane line tell you about changing lanes?
sec04-F06-card.expected_back: A solid white lane line calls for staying in the lane unless a special circumstance requires a change.

sec04-F07-card.front: Where must your vehicle come to rest when a sign or traffic signal requires a stop?
sec04-F07-card.expected_back: For a stop required by a sign or signal, stop before the vehicle reaches the stop line or crosswalk.

sec04-F08-card.front: What specific roadway function does a crosswalk identify?
sec04-F08-card.expected_back: A crosswalk identifies the place where pedestrians cross the road.

sec04-F09-card.front: Which pedestrians at a crosswalk hold right-of-way over approaching vehicles?
sec04-F09-card.expected_back: Drivers must yield to pedestrians already in a crosswalk or about to step into it.

sec04-F10-card.front: Do painted white stripes have to be present for a legal pedestrian crossing to exist?
sec04-F10-card.expected_back: A pedestrian crossing can exist even without painted crosswalk markings.

sec04-F11-card.front: What kind of traffic flow do yellow lane lines divide?
sec04-F11-card.expected_back: Yellow lane lines separate vehicles moving toward each other.

sec04-F12-card.front: When are you allowed to overtake across a single broken yellow center line?
sec04-F12-card.expected_back: A broken yellow center line permits passing when the maneuver is safe.

sec04-F13-card.front: What is the passing rule when a solid yellow line sits next to your lane alongside a broken yellow line?
sec04-F13-card.expected_back: With a paired solid and broken yellow center line, a driver on the solid-line side may not pass.

sec04-F14-card.front: When paired solid and broken yellow center lines divide the road, what may a driver beside the broken line do?
sec04-F14-card.expected_back: With a paired solid and broken yellow center line, a driver beside the broken line may pass when safe.

sec04-F15-card.front: What passing rule applies when a double solid yellow line runs down the center of the road?
sec04-F15-card.expected_back: A double solid yellow center line prohibits passing from either side.

sec04-F16-card.front: When is turning left across a solid yellow stripe into a private entrance allowed?
sec04-F16-card.expected_back: A driver may cross a solid yellow line to enter a driveway when the turn is safe.

sec04-R14-card.front: Which maneuvers are permitted from a shared center lane, and which directions of traffic may enter it?
sec04-R14-card.expected_back: A shared center lane is reserved for left turns and permitted U-turns, and vehicles from either direction may use it for those turns.

sec04-R15-card.front: What pavement symbols show the allowed movements inside a shared middle turn lane?
sec04-R15-card.expected_back: Alternating left-turn arrows show the movements permitted from a shared middle lane.

sec04-R16-card.front: How are both outer edges of a shared middle turn lane painted?
sec04-R16-card.expected_back: A shared middle lane is bounded on each side by a solid yellow line paired with a broken yellow line.

sec04-R01-card.front: How does traffic direction work inside a reversible lane?
sec04-R01-card.expected_back: A reversible lane carries traffic in opposite directions at different times.

sec04-R02-card.front: What yellow pavement markings commonly border a reversible lane?
sec04-R02-card.expected_back: Reversible lanes are commonly marked by paired broken yellow lines.

sec04-R03-card.front: What must you check before steering into any reversible lane?
sec04-R03-card.expected_back: Before entering a reversible lane, check the current lane-use signs or signals.

sec04-R04-card.front: What does a green arrow shining directly above a traffic lane mean?
sec04-R04-card.expected_back: A green overhead arrow permits use of the lane directly below it.

sec04-R05-card.front: What does a red X displayed above a lane command drivers to do?
sec04-R05-card.expected_back: A red overhead X prohibits driving in the lane below it.

sec04-R06-card.front: How may you use a lane when a flashing yellow X shines overhead?
sec04-R06-card.expected_back: A flashing yellow overhead X limits the lane to turning.

sec04-R07-card.front: What does a steady yellow X above your lane warn, and what action must you take?
sec04-R07-card.expected_back: A steady yellow overhead X warns of a lane-use change and calls for leaving the lane as soon as safe.

sec04-R08-card.front: How do roadways identify a lane set aside for special vehicles or uses?
sec04-R08-card.expected_back: A reserved lane is identified by signs describing the permitted use and often by a white diamond.

sec04-R09-card.front: Which vehicles are allowed to travel in a lane marked Transit or Bus?
sec04-R09-card.expected_back: A lane labeled Transit or Bus is reserved for buses.

sec04-R10-card.front: Who is a roadway lane labeled Bicycle reserved for?
sec04-R10-card.expected_back: A lane labeled Bicycle is reserved for bicycle travel.

sec04-R11-card.front: What does H O V stand for, and what basic requirement defines an H O V lane?
sec04-R11-card.expected_back: HOV means high-occupancy vehicles and identifies a lane for vehicles carrying more than one person.

sec04-R12-card.front: What three pieces of rule information appear on an H O V lane sign?
sec04-R12-card.expected_back: The sign for an HOV lane specifies the required occupancy and the days and hours of the restriction.

sec04-R13-card.front: How many people must be inside your vehicle when a lane posts an H O V three sign?
sec04-R13-card.expected_back: An HOV three sign requires at least three occupants in the vehicle.

sec04-R17-card.front: Why must you double-check controls before entering a shared middle lane during peak traffic periods?
sec04-R17-card.expected_back: Some shared middle lanes become reversible during peak traffic periods, so entry requires checking that the lane is available and safe.

sec04-R18-card.front: What governs which lane you should use when no specific lane-use signs or markings are present?
sec04-R18-card.expected_back: When signs and markings do not assign lane use, general driving, passing and turning rules determine the lane to use.

sec05-F01-card.front: Under what lone exception is backing inside a New Mexico travel lane permitted?
sec05-F01-card.expected_back: Backing within a travel lane is prohibited except when parallel parking.

sec05-F02-card.front: What should you do right after missing your street turn or highway exit?
sec05-F02-card.expected_back: After missing a turn or exit, continue ahead until a safe place allows you to turn around.

sec05-F03-card.front: How should you handle confusion, car trouble, or letting a passenger out instead of halting in-lane?
sec05-F03-card.expected_back: Do not stop in a travel lane for confusion, a breakdown or a passenger exit; continue until you can pull off safely.

sec05-F04-card.front: Which lane should you use on a road with two or more same-direction lanes?
sec05-F04-card.expected_back: Where at least two lanes carry traffic the same way, use the right lane except when passing.

sec05-F05-card.front: Which lane should you pick on a three-or-more-lane road with heavy entering and exiting traffic?
sec05-F05-card.expected_back: Where at least three lanes carry traffic the same way and entering or exiting vehicles are numerous, use the center travel lane.

sec05-F06-card.front: When are you allowed to drive along a roadway shoulder?
sec05-F06-card.expected_back: Use the roadway shoulder only when officials direct you to drive there.

sec05-F07-card.front: What is the intended purpose of the far-left lane on a multilane roadway?
sec05-F07-card.expected_back: On a multilane road, the far-left lane is intended for overtaking slower vehicles.

sec05-F08-card.front: What visibility danger arises whenever you overtake another vehicle on its right side?
sec05-F08-card.expected_back: When you overtake on the right, the other driver may have trouble seeing you and could move into your path.

sec05-F09-card.front: Does paving a road shoulder make it legal to use for overtaking?
sec05-F09-card.expected_back: Passing on the shoulder is prohibited whether the shoulder is paved or unpaved.

sec05-F10-card.front: From which lane do you start and into which lane do you finish an unmarked turn?
sec05-F10-card.expected_back: When signs or markings do not control a turn, start from the lane nearest the intended direction and enter the lane nearest the one you left.

sec05-F11-card.front: What path should your wheels follow between lanes while turning?
sec05-F11-card.expected_back: During a turn, take the most direct feasible path between lanes without crossing lane lines or interfering with traffic.

sec05-F12-card.front: When should you move into a different lane if your destination sits beyond the nearest turn lane?
sec05-F12-card.expected_back: After completing a turn, you may change lanes if needed.

sec05-F13-card.front: How often must you use your turn signals for turns and lane changes?
sec05-F13-card.expected_back: Signal every turn and every lane change.

sec05-F14-card.front: What steering habit must you avoid right before making a right turn?
sec05-F14-card.expected_back: Before a right turn, avoid swinging widely to the left.

sec05-R01-card.front: How can swinging left before a right turn trap a driver following behind you?
sec05-R01-card.expected_back: A wide leftward swing before a right turn can look like a lane change or left turn and prompt a following driver to pass on your right.

sec05-R02-card.front: Why is drifting out into a farther lane while finishing a right turn hazardous?
sec05-R02-card.expected_back: Swinging into a farther lane while completing a right turn can surprise drivers already in that lane.

sec05-R03-card.front: What crash risk comes from slicing across the corner too early during a left turn?
sec05-R03-card.expected_back: During a left turn, avoid cutting across the corner into the path of a vehicle approaching from the left.

sec05-R04-card.front: Where must you leave room for an oncoming driver who is also turning left?
sec05-R04-card.expected_back: A left-turning driver must leave enough room for opposing traffic to turn left ahead of the vehicle.

sec05-R05-card.front: What lane rule governs intersections where signs or paint establish multiple turning lanes?
sec05-R05-card.expected_back: When signs or lane markings allow multiple turning lanes, remain within your assigned lane through the turn.

sec06-F01-card.front: What do right-of-way rules clarify when vehicles or pedestrians meet without traffic controls?
sec06-F01-card.expected_back: At an uncontrolled meeting of vehicles or pedestrians, right-of-way rules identify who yields and who waits.

sec06-F02-card.front: Does New Mexico law grant an absolute right to go, or does it assign a different responsibility?
sec06-F02-card.expected_back: The law assigns a duty to yield rather than granting an absolute right to proceed.

sec06-F03-card.front: How far must you go to avoid striking a pedestrian or another vehicle in any situation?
sec06-F03-card.expected_back: A driver must take every possible action to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle regardless of the situation.

sec06-F04-card.front: What must you do when a pedestrian steps out while disobeying a traffic control?
sec06-F04-card.expected_back: Yield to a pedestrian even when that pedestrian disobeys a traffic control.

sec06-F05-card.front: Who gets priority when your car crosses a sidewalk to enter or exit a driveway, alley, or lot?
sec06-F05-card.expected_back: When crossing a sidewalk to enter or leave a driveway, alley or parking lot, yield to pedestrians.

sec06-F06-card.front: When may your vehicle legally touch a sidewalk, and what sidewalk movement is banned?
sec06-F06-card.expected_back: Driving along a sidewalk is prohibited; crossing it is the permitted exception.

sec06-F07-card.front: Whose access to roads and sidewalks does the New Mexico White Cane Law protect?
sec06-F07-card.expected_back: The handbook describes the White Cane Law as protecting access to roads and sidewalks for people who are blind, visually impaired or otherwise physically disabled.

sec06-F08-card.front: Which New Mexico statute number does the handbook cite for the White Cane Law?
sec06-F08-card.expected_back: The handbook cites the White Cane Law as twenty-eight-seven-one NMSA (nineteen seventy-eight).

sec06-F09-card.front: What must you do when approaching a blind or partially blind pedestrian with a white or metallic cane or guide dog?
sec06-F09-card.expected_back: Take all necessary injury-prevention precautions when approaching a blind or partially blind pedestrian using a predominantly white or metallic cane, with or without a red tip, or a guide dog.

sec06-F10-card.front: What legal consequence hits a driver who skips injury-prevention precautions for a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog?
sec06-F10-card.expected_back: A driver who fails to take necessary injury-prevention precautions for a blind or partially blind pedestrian using a predominantly white or metallic cane, with or without a red tip, or a guide dog is liable for resulting injury damages.

sec06-F11-card.front: Who must yield when you want to turn left across oncoming vehicles continuing straight?
sec06-F11-card.expected_back: A left-turning driver yields to oncoming vehicles continuing straight.

sec06-F12-card.front: Who has priority before you pull into a traffic circle or rotary?
sec06-F12-card.expected_back: Before entering a traffic circle or rotary, yield to vehicles already circulating.

sec06-F13-card.front: Which vehicle gets priority at an intersection with no stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal?
sec06-F13-card.expected_back: At an intersection lacking a stop sign, yield sign or traffic signal, give priority to vehicles approaching from the right.

sec06-F14-card.front: When vehicles reach a four-way stop at different times, who proceeds first and after what action?
sec06-F14-card.expected_back: At a four-way stop, the first vehicle to arrive goes first after making a complete stop.

sec06-F15-card.front: Who goes first when two vehicles stop at a four-way intersection at the exact same moment?
sec06-F15-card.expected_back: When vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, the vehicle to the right goes first.

sec06-F16-card.front: Who must yield when pulling onto a street from a driveway, alley, or roadside?
sec06-F16-card.expected_back: A driver joining a road from a driveway, alley or roadside yields to vehicles on the main road.

sec06-F17-card.front: When backed-up traffic fills the far side of an intersection, where must you wait?
sec06-F17-card.expected_back: Wait outside an intersection until the space beyond lets you cross it without stopping inside.

sec06-R01-card.front: What yielding rule applies when you overtake a vehicle traveling in the same direction, even if it slows or stops?
sec06-R01-card.expected_back: A driver overtaking another vehicle moving in the same direction must yield to that vehicle even when it slows or stops.

sec06-R02-card.front: Which active audible or visual signals require you to yield to an emergency vehicle?
sec06-R02-card.expected_back: Yield to an emergency vehicle operating a siren, air horn, or flashing red or blue light.

sec06-R03-card.front: Where should you position your car when an active emergency vehicle approaches from any direction?
sec06-R03-card.expected_back: For an emergency vehicle approaching from any direction while using a siren, air horn, or flashing red or blue light, pull to the right edge or as near to it as possible.

sec06-R04-card.front: What must you do if an emergency crew broadcasts directions over a vehicle loudspeaker?
sec06-R04-card.expected_back: Follow instructions broadcast through an emergency vehicle’s loudspeaker.

sec06-R05-card.front: What should you do first if an active emergency vehicle approaches while you are already inside an intersection?
sec06-R05-card.expected_back: When yielding to an emergency vehicle using a siren, air horn, or flashing red or blue light, clear the intersection before pulling over if you are already inside it.

sec06-R06-card.front: When must you stop for a stopped school bus flashing red lights, and what is the sole oncoming exception?
sec06-R06-card.expected_back: Stop for a stopped school bus with flashing red lights on either side of the road or at an approaching intersection, except when an oncoming bus is separated from your roadway by a median or another physical barrier.

sec06-R07-card.front: When are oncoming drivers exempt from stopping for a school bus with flashing red lights?
sec06-R07-card.expected_back: The stop rule for a school bus with flashing red lights does not apply when the bus faces you across a median or other physical barrier separating the roadways.

sec06-R08-card.front: Once a school bus turns off its flashing red lights, how long must you still remain stopped?
sec06-R08-card.expected_back: After school-bus red lights stop flashing, remain stopped until children are completely off the roadway and proceeding is safe.

sec06-R09-card.front: Between road vehicles and a train crossing the roadway, who always yields?
sec06-R09-card.expected_back: Yield to a train crossing the roadway.

sec06-R10-card.front: What must the state post whenever it designates a public road for one-way traffic?
sec06-R10-card.expected_back: If the state makes a public road one-way, it must post signs identifying that direction.

sec06-R11-card.front: How must you travel once you are on a signed one-way road?
sec06-R11-card.expected_back: On a signed one-way road, drive only in the indicated direction.

sec06-R12-card.front: Which side of the central island must you stay on while driving around a traffic circle or rotary?
sec06-R12-card.expected_back: When driving around a traffic circle or rotary island, keep to the island’s right side.

sec08-F01-card.front: Why is reading a driver manual alone not enough to learn safe driving?
sec08-F01-card.expected_back: Learning to drive safely requires instruction and practice beyond reading a manual.

sec08-F02-card.front: Which guide should you check for your specific vehicle's proper starting procedure?
sec08-F02-card.expected_back: Use the vehicle owner’s manual for the proper starting procedure.

sec08-F03-card.front: What brake check must you confirm before starting the engine?
sec08-F03-card.expected_back: Before starting the vehicle, make sure its parking brake is applied.

sec08-F04-card.front: What gear state must a manual-transmission vehicle be in before starting?
sec08-F04-card.expected_back: A manual-transmission vehicle must be out of gear before starting.

sec08-F05-card.front: What extra pedal step do some manual-transmission vehicles require before the starter engages?
sec08-F05-card.expected_back: Some manual-transmission vehicles also require pressing the clutch before starting.

sec08-F06-card.front: Which gear position should you select before starting an automatic-transmission vehicle?
sec08-F06-card.expected_back: Before starting an automatic-transmission vehicle, select Park.

sec08-F07-card.front: How should you build speed when pulling away instead of stomping the gas?
sec08-F07-card.expected_back: Build speed smoothly rather than accelerating abruptly.

sec08-F08-card.front: What happens to your driving wheels if you make a sudden start, especially on a slick road?
sec08-F08-card.expected_back: A sudden start can spin the driving wheels and make the vehicle slide, especially on a slick surface.

sec08-F09-card.front: Which two pedals must you practice coordinating on a manual car to prevent stalling or over-revving?
sec08-F09-card.expected_back: With a manual transmission, practice coordinating clutch and accelerator to avoid over-revving or stalling during gear changes.

sec08-F10-card.front: How should your hands grip the steering wheel during normal driving?
sec08-F10-card.expected_back: Grip the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides in a balanced position.

sec08-F11-card.front: Which primary clock-face hand position does the staged New Mexico handbook present as a balanced grip?
sec08-F11-card.expected_back: The staged handbook presents the ten-and-two clock positions as a balanced steering grip.

sec08-F12-card.front: Which second clock-face hand position does the handbook describe as an alternative balanced grip?
sec08-F12-card.expected_back: The handbook also describes the nine-and-three clock positions as an alternative grip.

sec08-F13-card.front: Where should your knuckles stay relative to the steering-wheel rim?
sec08-F13-card.expected_back: Keep your knuckles on the outside of the steering-wheel rim.

sec08-F14-card.front: Where should you aim your eyes so you spot upcoming steering adjustments early?
sec08-F14-card.expected_back: Look far ahead and toward both roadsides so upcoming steering needs can be recognized early.

sec08-F15-card.front: Which steering technique does the handbook describe for turning around a sharp corner?
sec08-F15-card.expected_back: For a sharp corner, the handbook describes using hand-over-hand steering.

sec08-F16-card.front: How should you bring the steering wheel back to straight after finishing a turn?
sec08-F16-card.expected_back: After completing a turn, guide the wheel back to straight by hand.

sec08-F17-card.front: Why should you avoid letting the steering wheel spin freely back through your fingers?
sec08-F17-card.expected_back: Allowing the steering wheel to slide through your fingers can be dangerous.

sec08-F18-card.front: Why must you glance at your speedometer frequently instead of trusting how fast the car feels?
sec08-F18-card.expected_back: Check the speedometer frequently because a driver’s sense of speed is unreliable.

sec08-F19-card.front: What speed-judgment error commonly traps drivers right after exiting a fast highway onto a slower local street?
sec08-F19-card.expected_back: After leaving a fast road for a slower local road, a driver can underestimate the vehicle’s speed.

sec08-F20-card.front: What straightforward rule applies to posted speed-limit signs along your route?

sec08-F21-card.front: How should you time your search for stopping situations ahead?
sec08-F21-card.expected_back: Look for the need to stop early instead of waiting for a last-second response.

sec08-F22-card.front: What vehicle-control danger can abrupt braking trigger?
sec08-F22-card.expected_back: Abrupt braking can produce a skid and loss of vehicle control.

sec08-F23-card.front: How does a sudden stop affect drivers traveling behind your vehicle?
sec08-F23-card.expected_back: A sudden stop makes it harder for following drivers to stop without hitting your vehicle.

sec08-F24-card.front: What smoother options replace a panic stop when you recognize road hazards early?
sec08-F24-card.expected_back: Recognizing hazards early allows a gradual slowdown or lane change instead of a panic stop.

sec08-F25-card.front: Which directions around your car must you continuously scan to stay aware of traffic events?
sec08-F25-card.expected_back: Scan in front, on both sides and behind the vehicle to stay aware of surrounding events.

sec08-F26-card.front: How does active scanning protect you from people or vehicles near your travel lane?
sec08-F26-card.expected_back: Scanning helps identify people or vehicles that could enter your path before you reach them.

sec08-F27-card.front: Besides people and vehicles, what crucial roadside information does steady scanning uncover?
sec08-F27-card.expected_back: Scanning also reveals warning signs and route directions.

sec08-F28-card.front: How does looking well ahead change your steering and braking inputs?
sec08-F28-card.expected_back: Looking well ahead reduces the need for a last-moment turn or brake application.

sec08-F29-card.front: What two everyday benefits come from looking well ahead besides crash prevention?
sec08-F29-card.expected_back: Looking well ahead can help conserve fuel and keep traffic movement steady.

sec08-F30-card.front: How does far-ahead scanning improve the way your car tracks inside its lane?
sec08-F30-card.expected_back: Far-ahead scanning helps a driver steer with less weaving.

sec08-F31-card.front: At least how many seconds ahead does the New Mexico handbook say safer drivers tend to look?
sec08-F31-card.expected_back: The handbook says safer drivers tend to look at least ten seconds ahead.

sec08-F32-card.front: In city traffic, roughly what physical distance equals the handbook's ten-second look-ahead?
sec08-F32-card.expected_back: In city traffic, the handbook’s ten-second look-ahead distance is approximately one block.

sec08-F33-card.front: How far ahead does the handbook recommend scanning while driving in the city?
sec08-F33-card.expected_back: The handbook recommends looking at least a block ahead in city driving.

sec08-F34-card.front: Where is looking toward both sides for entering vehicles or walkers especially critical?
sec08-F34-card.expected_back: Look toward both sides for entering vehicles or pedestrians, especially near intersections and railroad crossings.

sec08-F35-card.front: What broad range of locations counts as an intersection according to the handbook?
sec08-F35-card.expected_back: An intersection is any point where traffic paths join or cross, including streets, driveways and parking-lot entrances.

sec08-F36-card.front: Which directions must you check for traffic and pedestrians before entering any intersection?
sec08-F36-card.expected_back: Before entering an intersection, look left and right for traffic and pedestrians.

sec08-F37-card.front: After making a full stop at an intersection, what must you do right before accelerating?
sec08-F37-card.expected_back: After stopping at an intersection, look both ways again just before moving.

sec08-F38-card.front: What must you verify about your entire crossing path before rolling into an intersection?
sec08-F38-card.expected_back: Before moving into an intersection, confirm the entire crossing path is clear so a stop will not block it.

sec08-F39-card.front: What visibility check is mandatory before committing your vehicle into an intersection?
sec08-F39-card.expected_back: Before entering an intersection, make sure you can clearly see traffic crossing your path.

sec08-R01-card.front: What must you wait for before turning left across approaching traffic?
sec08-R01-card.expected_back: Before turning left across approaching traffic, wait for a gap large enough to complete the movement safely.

sec08-R02-card.front: Why must you scan the destination street before starting a left turn across oncoming lanes?
sec08-R02-card.expected_back: Before turning left, check the destination street for vehicles or pedestrians that could leave you stranded in the opposing traffic path.

sec08-R03-card.front: Where should your eyes look one final time immediately before turning left across oncoming traffic?
sec08-R03-card.expected_back: Immediately before turning left across oncoming traffic, look once more toward the oncoming vehicles.

sec08-R04-card.front: Which approaching traffic stream must you check before turning right?
sec08-R04-card.expected_back: Before turning right, check for vehicles approaching from your left.

sec08-R05-card.front: What oncoming-vehicle movement must you watch for before turning right?
sec08-R05-card.expected_back: Before turning right, check whether an oncoming vehicle will turn left into your path.

sec08-R06-card.front: Where must you check for pedestrians before starting a right turn?
sec08-R06-card.expected_back: Check for pedestrians in the destination crossing before beginning a right turn.

sec08-R07-card.front: When is New Mexico's general permission to turn right on a red light canceled?
sec08-R07-card.expected_back: A posted prohibition overrides the handbook’s permission to turn right on red.

sec08-R08-card.front: When does the handbook permit turning left from one one-way street onto another one-way street?
sec08-R08-card.expected_back: The handbook permits a left turn from a one-way street into another one-way street unless the turn is prohibited.

sec08-R09-card.front: Why must you never assume a stop sign or red signal guarantees cross traffic will stop?
sec08-R09-card.expected_back: Do not assume a traffic sign or signal guarantees that cross traffic will stop.

sec08-R10-card.front: Should you still look left and right when cross traffic faces a stop sign or red light?
sec08-R10-card.expected_back: Look left and right at an intersection even when crossing traffic faces a red light or a stop sign.

sec08-R11-card.front: Why is extra caution needed right after your traffic signal turns green?
sec08-R11-card.expected_back: Use particular care just after a light turns green because cross traffic may still try to hurry through.

sec08-R12-card.front: How should you proceed after stopping if hedges, walls, or parked vehicles block your cross-street view?
sec08-R12-card.expected_back: If your cross-street view is blocked after stopping, creep forward slowly until approaching traffic becomes visible.

sec08-R13-card.front: How does edging forward slowly help cross-street drivers when a corner view is obstructed?
sec08-R13-card.expected_back: Moving forward slowly can let crossing drivers notice the vehicle’s front and give them a chance to slow or warn you.

sec08-R14-card.front: Which roadside environments demand extra scanning because people may step suddenly into the street?
sec08-R14-card.expected_back: Scan the roadside carefully near shops, parking lots, road work, busy sidewalks, playgrounds and schoolyards because people may enter the road there.

sec08-R15-card.front: What two actions must you take at every railroad crossing approach?
sec08-R15-card.expected_back: At every railroad approach, reduce speed and look both ways along the tracks for a train.

sec08-R16-card.front: How should you treat a familiar railroad crossing where you have never seen a train?
sec08-R16-card.expected_back: A crossing where you have never seen a train must still be checked for an approaching train.

sec08-R17-card.front: What space check must pass before you start driving across railroad tracks?
sec08-R17-card.expected_back: Cross tracks only when enough room exists beyond them to hold the vehicle.

sec08-R18-card.front: Why must you wait until a passing train moves well down the line at a multitrack crossing?
sec08-R18-card.expected_back: At a multitrack crossing, let a passing train move well away before crossing because it can hide another train.

sec08-R19-card.front: How should your mirror-checking pace change when traffic volume turns heavy?
sec08-R19-card.expected_back: Monitor rear traffic more frequently when the traffic stream is heavy.

sec08-R20-card.front: What two dangerous following behaviors do regular rear checks reveal?
sec08-R20-card.expected_back: Rear checks reveal a following vehicle that is too close or approaching too quickly.

sec08-R21-card.front: Before which four maneuvers or road features are rear-traffic checks especially important?
sec08-R21-card.expected_back: Rear-traffic checks are especially important before a lane change, slowdown, backing movement or descent of a long or steep hill.

sec08-R22-card.front: Which two zones must you check for vehicles in the target lane before changing lanes?
sec08-R22-card.expected_back: Before changing lanes, check both the side and the rear for vehicles in the intended lane.

sec08-R23-card.front: Besides moving between marked travel lanes, what two entries count as lane changes?
sec08-R23-card.expected_back: Lane changing includes merging from an entrance ramp and entering traffic from a curb or shoulder.

sec08-R24-card.front: Which mirrors should you use together to check whether your target lane is clear?
sec08-R24-card.expected_back: Use both rearview and side mirrors to check whether the target lane is clear.

sec08-R25-card.front: What passing conflict must you rule out before drifting into an adjacent lane?
sec08-R25-card.expected_back: Before changing lanes, make sure another vehicle is not about to pass you.

sec08-R26-card.front: How do you check the spaces near your car's rear corners before moving sideways?
sec08-R26-card.expected_back: Before moving sideways, look over your shoulder toward that direction to check near the vehicle’s rear corners.

sec08-R27-card.front: What name describes the rear-corner zones around your car that mirrors cannot show?
sec08-R27-card.expected_back: The rear-corner areas invisible through the mirrors are blind spots.

sec08-R28-card.front: Why must your side and rear checks stay brief?
sec08-R28-card.expected_back: Side and rear checks should be brief because traffic ahead can stop unexpectedly while you look away.

sec08-R29-card.front: Why should you use mirrors first while preparing to merge, change lanes, or enter traffic?
sec08-R29-card.expected_back: Use mirrors while preparing to merge, change lanes or enter the road so you can continue monitoring ahead.

sec08-R30-card.front: When should you perform your over-the-shoulder blind-spot check for a lane change?
sec08-R30-card.expected_back: Check over your shoulder for blind-spot traffic immediately before changing lanes.

sec08-R31-card.front: Which is safer when checking away from the road ahead, one long stare or several quick looks?
sec08-R31-card.expected_back: Several quick looks are preferable to one long look away from the road ahead.

sec08-R32-card.front: Which two traffic streams must you keep tracking while actually changing lanes?
sec08-R32-card.expected_back: During a lane change, track both the traffic ahead and the traffic in the lane you are entering.

sec08-R33-card.front: On a road with three or more lanes, why must you check the lane beyond your target lane?
sec08-R33-card.expected_back: If there is a lane beyond the one you plan to enter, check it for another driver moving into the same space.

sec08-R34-card.front: Which three groups of road users are harder to spot than cars or trucks?
sec08-R34-card.expected_back: Motorcyclists, bicyclists and pedestrians can be harder to notice than cars or trucks.

sec08-R35-card.front: When must you be extra alert for cyclists, motorcyclists, and walkers along the road edge?
sec08-R35-card.expected_back: Be particularly alert for other road users when pulling into the roadway from a curb or driveway.

sec08-R36-card.front: When should slowing down trigger an immediate rear-traffic check, and when is that check most critical?
sec08-R36-card.expected_back: Check rear traffic whenever you slow, especially for a sudden slowdown or a stop at an unexpected driveway or parking space.

sec08-R37-card.front: Why should you keep backing movements to a minimum?
sec08-R37-card.expected_back: Keep backing movements to a minimum because the area behind a vehicle is difficult to see.

sec08-R38-card.front: How can smart stall choice in a parking lot eliminate backing out later?
sec08-R38-card.expected_back: A parking space that lets you drive through can allow a forward departure instead of backing out.

sec08-R39-card.front: What should you inspect behind your parked car before climbing in to back up?
sec08-R39-card.expected_back: Before entering the vehicle to back it, check behind for children or low objects hidden from the driver’s seat.

sec08-R40-card.front: What body position does the handbook describe for looking rearward while backing?
sec08-R40-card.expected_back: When backing, the handbook describes resting the right arm on the seatback and turning to look through the rear window.

sec08-R41-card.front: Why must you never rely solely on mirrors while backing up?
sec08-R41-card.expected_back: Do not rely only on the mirrors while backing because they do not show the area directly behind the vehicle.

sec08-R42-card.front: Why must you keep your speed very slow whenever reversing?
sec08-R42-card.expected_back: Reverse slowly because controlling the steering is harder while moving backward.

sec08-R43-card.front: Who should you ask for help during a tricky backing movement whenever available?
sec08-R43-card.expected_back: Use a person outside to help guide a backing movement whenever possible.

sec08-R44-card.front: What should you watch for in your mirrors during a long or steep downhill descent?
sec08-R44-card.expected_back: During a long or steep descent, watch the mirrors for vehicles gaining speed behind you.

sec08-R45-card.front: Which specific vehicles behind you demand extra downhill alertness if they approach too fast?
sec08-R45-card.expected_back: On downhill grades, stay alert for large trucks or buses approaching too fast.

sec11-F01-card.front: What safety advantage do you gain by keeping more space between your vehicle and other road users?
sec11-F01-card.expected_back: More separation from other road users gives you additional time to respond.

sec11-F02-card.front: What crash type commonly results from following too closely when the vehicle ahead brakes suddenly?
sec11-F02-card.expected_back: Following too close can cause a rear-end collision when the leading vehicle stops suddenly.

sec11-F03-card.front: How do you use a fixed roadside object to measure the three-second following gap?
sec11-F03-card.expected_back: For the three-second following check, note when the leading vehicle’s rear passes a fixed roadside marker, then count until you reach that marker.

sec11-F04-card.front: What does it mean if your front bumper reaches the roadside marker before you finish counting three seconds?
sec11-F04-card.expected_back: If you reach the following-distance marker before completing three seconds, you are too close.

sec11-F05-card.front: How should you correct your position after failing a three-second following check?
sec11-F05-card.expected_back: Increase the gap and repeat the following-distance check until at least three seconds separate you.

sec11-F06-card.front: How many seconds of following gap does the New Mexico manual suggest on slippery pavement or behind a motorcycle?
sec11-F06-card.expected_back: The manual gives a four-second following gap as a potentially needed increase on slippery roads or behind a motorcycle.

sec11-F07-card.front: What following interval does the manual list as an example when pulling a heavy trailer or trailing an emergency vehicle?
sec11-F07-card.expected_back: A heavy load or trailer, or following an emergency vehicle, can require a four-second following gap in the manual’s examples.

sec11-F08-card.front: Which two roadway or grade situations also appear in the handbook's four-second following-space examples?
sec11-F08-card.expected_back: The handbook also lists approaching railroad crossings and being stopped on a hill or incline as situations that may need four seconds of following space.

sec11-F09-card.front: What two habits help a driver behind you maintain a safe following cushion?
sec11-F09-card.expected_back: Maintain steady speed and signal slowing or turning early to help a following driver keep a safe gap.

sec11-F10-card.front: Why should you keep open space beside your vehicle on both sides whenever traffic allows?
sec11-F10-card.expected_back: Keep space on each side so you have room to turn or change lanes.

sec11-F11-card.front: How should you position your car on a road with two or more lanes when traffic is entering?
sec11-F11-card.expected_back: On a road with at least two lanes, make room for vehicles entering.

sec11-F12-card.front: How should you adjust your lane position when driving past a line of parked cars?
sec11-F12-card.expected_back: Allow additional side space beside parked cars.

sec11-F13-card.front: Who deserves extra side clearance along the roadway, and which age group needs special vigilance?
sec11-F13-card.memory_hook: Wide room for walkers, cyclists, kids
sec11-F13-card.expected_back: Give pedestrians and cyclists extra space, with particular care around children.

sec11-F14-card.front: Roughly how many seconds of traffic gap does the New Mexico handbook specify for merging?
sec11-F14-card.expected_back: The handbook specifies a gap of about four seconds when merging with traffic.

sec11-F15-card.front: When you pull squarely into the middle of a four-second traffic gap, what buffers remain ahead and behind?
sec11-F15-card.expected_back: Entering halfway into a four-second gap leaves roughly two seconds ahead and two seconds behind.

sec11-F16-card.front: To which three everyday traffic movements does the handbook apply its four-second merge gap?
sec11-F16-card.expected_back: The handbook applies its four-second merge gap to lane changes, roadway entry and a lane joining another lane.

sec11-F17-card.front: What rule applies when the opening beside you is smaller than a safe merging gap?
sec11-F17-card.expected_back: Do not force a merge into insufficient space.

sec11-F18-card.front: How must you move across a multi-lane roadway when shifting over several lanes?
sec11-F18-card.expected_back: When crossing multiple lanes, move across one lane at a time.

sec11-F19-card.front: How big must a traffic gap be before you drive straight across an intersecting roadway?
sec11-F19-card.expected_back: Crossing traffic requires a gap large enough to clear the entire roadway.

sec11-F20-card.front: Beyond room for the turn itself, what else must your gap allow when turning into moving traffic?
sec11-F20-card.expected_back: Entering traffic requires enough room to complete the turn and accelerate.

sec11-F21-card.front: Before starting a left turn, what two potential blockers must be clear of your target path?
sec11-F21-card.expected_back: Before a left turn, verify that neither vehicles nor pedestrians obstruct your path.

sec11-F22-card.front: Does a green traffic light allow you to pull into an intersection when backed-up cars block the far side?
sec11-F22-card.expected_back: A green signal does not justify starting across when vehicles block your route.

sec11-F23-card.front: When is it legal and safe to drive onto a railroad crossing behind slow traffic?
sec11-F23-card.expected_back: Enter railroad tracks only with sufficient space to clear them without stopping on the rails.

sec11-R01-card.front: Do dashed centerlines or passing-zone signs guarantee that overtaking right now is safe?
sec11-R01-card.expected_back: Even where markings or signs allow passing, independently judge whether enough space makes the maneuver safe.

sec11-R02-card.front: How many vehicles should you overtake in a single pass as a general rule?
sec11-R02-card.expected_back: As a general practice, overtake one vehicle at a time rather than assuming room to pass several.

sec11-R03-card.front: At fifty-five miles per hour, roughly how long does a pass take according to the New Mexico handbook?
sec11-R03-card.expected_back: At fifty-five miles per hour, the handbook estimates about ten seconds to pass, requiring corresponding oncoming-traffic and sight-distance gaps.

sec11-R04-card.front: How far ahead must your view stay clear when passing near hills or curves?
sec11-R04-card.expected_back: For passing near hills and curves, the source requires visibility of at least one-third mile, described as about ten seconds ahead.

sec11-R05-card.front: What must you always assume whenever a hill crest or curve blocks your forward view?
sec11-R05-card.expected_back: When a curve or hill blocks the view, assume an approaching vehicle could be hidden beyond it.

sec11-R06-card.front: Within what distance of an approaching hill or curve must you never start a pass?
sec11-R06-card.expected_back: Do not begin passing within one-third mile of a hill or curve.

sec11-R07-card.front: Why is passing hazardous near intersections, railroad tracks, and shopping-center driveways?
sec11-R07-card.expected_back: Passing is hazardous at intersections, railroad crossings and shopping entrances where another road user may enter or cross.

sec11-R08-card.front: What three major hazards can the vehicle you are overtaking hide from your sight?
sec11-R08-card.memory_hook: Lead car hides people, trains, cars
sec11-R08-card.expected_back: The vehicle being overtaken can hide people, vehicles or trains from your view.

sec11-R09-card.front: How can a side-street driver turning right create a sudden threat while you pass in the opposing lane?
sec11-R09-card.expected_back: Drivers turning right into the lane you use to pass may not expect you there or check your direction.

sec11-R10-card.front: What roadside situations should you scan for before overtaking in case another vehicle swerves sideways?
sec11-R10-card.expected_back: Before overtaking, scan for conditions that may push other road users into your intended lane.

sec11-R11-card.front: How do pedestrians or cyclists along the road edge affect your ability to overtake?
sec11-R11-card.expected_back: Pedestrians or cyclists near the roadway can reduce the space available for passing.

sec11-R12-card.front: Which structure widths or pavement flaws can wipe out safe room to pass?
sec11-R12-card.expected_back: A narrow bridge, reduced lane width, ice, potholes or roadway debris can remove passing room.

sec11-R13-card.front: What must already exist ahead of the vehicle you overtake before you pull out to pass?
sec11-R13-card.expected_back: Pass only when room exists to return to the driving lane; do not rely on others to create that room.

sec11-R14-card.front: What is the rule on overtaking when a railroad grade crossing lies ahead?
sec11-R14-card.expected_back: Do not overtake with a railroad grade crossing ahead.

sec11-R15-card.front: What visual check in your rearview mirror confirms safe clearance to pull back into the right lane after passing?
sec11-R15-card.expected_back: Before returning after passing, leave enough clearance; the manual’s visual cue is seeing both headlights of the passed vehicle in the rearview mirror.

sec12-F01-card.front: How do a bicyclist's legal rights and duties on New Mexico roads compare with a car driver's?
sec12-F01-card.expected_back: On roads, bicycle operators have the rights and responsibilities of car drivers.

sec12-F02-card.front: How much lateral clearance does the New Mexico handbook tell drivers to aim for when overtaking a cyclist?
sec12-F02-card.expected_back: When overtaking a cyclist, keep safe clearance, aim for at least five feet, and pass only where safe and legal.

sec12-F03-card.front: How should you respond when a cyclist ahead signals to merge across or enter a turn lane?
sec12-F03-card.expected_back: Allow cyclists additional space and time to merge or use a turn lane.

sec12-F04-card.front: What piece of lawful equipment does the handbook compare a bicycle to when sharing traffic lanes?
sec12-F04-card.expected_back: Treat a bicycle as a lawful slow vehicle, as you would a backhoe.

sec12-F05-card.front: Even though cyclists normally ride right, what lane position may they legally take when needed?
sec12-F05-card.expected_back: Although cyclists usually stay right, they may lawfully use the lane’s center and occupy the entire lane when necessary.

sec12-F06-card.front: What three everyday situations justify a bicyclist riding down the middle of the full lane?
sec12-F06-card.expected_back: Typical reasons for a cyclist to occupy the full lane include preparing to turn left, avoiding a squeeze on a narrow street, or avoiding grates, debris and other hazards.

sec12-F07-card.front: How must you execute a right turn when a bicyclist is riding alongside on your right?
sec12-F07-card.expected_back: With a cyclist on your right, avoid passing then making a sudden right turn; slow and merge behind the cyclist before turning.

sec12-F08-card.front: Which group of cyclists is especially likely to make unexpected lane shifts or sudden turns?
sec12-F08-card.expected_back: Expect unexpected movement or lane changes from some cyclists, particularly young children.

sec12-F09-card.front: How do stop signs, red lights, and traffic laws apply to bicyclists on the road?
sec12-F09-card.expected_back: Cyclists must follow traffic signals, signs and laws as car drivers do.

sec12-F10-card.front: What front and rear visibility equipment does the New Mexico handbook require on a bicycle at night?
sec12-F10-card.expected_back: The bicycle requirements described by the handbook include a bright front light and effective rear reflector at night.

sec12-F11-card.front: In what direction must cyclists ride, and how should they execute intersection turns?
sec12-F11-card.memory_hook: Ride with traffic, turn like cars
sec12-F11-card.expected_back: Cyclists must ride with traffic and make turns in the same manner as cars.

sec12-F12-card.front: How must bicyclists communicate upcoming turns and stops to surrounding traffic?
sec12-F12-card.memory_hook: Signal turns and stops by hand
sec12-F12-card.expected_back: The handbook requires cyclists to signal turns and stops by hand, with the gestures shown in its illustrations.

sec12-F13-card.front: What three practical habits help a cyclist stay noticeable to motorists?
sec12-F13-card.expected_back: Cyclists can improve conspicuity through bright clothing, suitable lighting and predictable movement.

sec12-F14-card.front: Which riding direction does the New Mexico manual identify as the safest position for a bicycle in traffic?
sec12-F14-card.expected_back: The source describes riding with the ordinary flow of traffic as the safest bicycle position in traffic.

sec12-F15-card.front: How does the New Mexico handbook's helmet guidance differ between adult riders and minors?
sec12-F15-card.expected_back: The manual advises well-fitting helmets for adults and states that minors must wear them.

sec12-F16-card.front: What do sharrow pavement markings designate on a street?
sec12-F16-card.expected_back: Sharrows are pavement symbols marking shared travel lanes.

sec12-F17-card.front: On what kind of street width are sharrows painted?
sec12-F17-card.expected_back: The handbook places sharrows where a road is too narrow for side-by-side sharing with slower vehicles.

sec12-F18-card.front: What does a sharrow encourage bicyclists to do, and what does it require from drivers?
sec12-F18-card.expected_back: A sharrow encourages cyclists to use the full lane and requires motorists to yield when needed.

sec12-F19-card.front: How should you adjust your driving when catching up to a cyclist on a sharrow-marked street?
sec12-F19-card.expected_back: At sharrows, motorists should reduce speed and yield to cyclists occupying the roadway.

sec12-F20-card.front: When may a motorist overtake a cyclist along a route with sharrows?
sec12-F20-card.memory_hook: Only where width lets rider right
sec12-F20-card.expected_back: At sharrows, pass a cyclist only when roadway width permits the cyclist to move right.

sec12-F21-card.front: How much passing clearance does the handbook's sharrow guidance ask motorists to aim for?
sec12-F21-card.expected_back: The sharrow guidance asks motorists to try for at least five feet of passing clearance.

sec12-F22-card.front: Where on the painted sharrow symbol is a bicyclist allowed to ride?
sec12-F22-card.expected_back: A cyclist may ride down the sharrow’s center.

sec12-F23-card.front: What curbside hazard zone does the sharrow section warn bicyclists to stay clear of?
sec12-F23-card.expected_back: Cyclists should keep clear of the area where a parked car’s door may open.

sec12-F24-card.front: When should a cyclist move toward the right to let trailing traffic pass?
sec12-F24-card.expected_back: Cyclists should move right to allow a vehicle past when doing so is safe.

sec12-R01-card.front: How does stopping distance for a large truck or RV compare with a passenger car at identical speed?
sec12-R01-card.expected_back: A large truck or RV requires more stopping distance than a car at the same speed.

sec12-R02-card.front: In the New Mexico handbook's fifty-five-mile-per-hour example, compare stopping distance for an average car versus a large truck?
sec12-R02-card.memory_hook: Car four hundred, truck eight hundred
sec12-R02-card.expected_back: In the manual’s fifty-five miles per hour comparison, an average car stops in about four hundred feet while a large truck may need almost eight hundred feet.

sec12-R03-card.front: Why must you never pull in front of a heavy truck and suddenly slow down or stop?
sec12-R03-card.expected_back: Do not pull ahead of a big truck and abruptly slow or stop; it may be unable to stop before striking you.

sec12-R04-card.front: How do large trucks and RVs handle tight corners, especially right turns?
sec12-R04-card.expected_back: Trucks and RVs need extra turning room and may swing wide for a right turn.

sec12-R05-card.front: What must you inspect on a large vehicle ahead before starting to overtake it?
sec12-R05-card.expected_back: Before passing a large vehicle you are following, inspect its turn signals.

sec12-R06-card.front: If a truck ahead drifts left as if turning left, why must you wait and recheck its blinkers?
sec12-R06-card.expected_back: If a truck appears to turn left, pause and recheck its signals because it may actually be setting up a right turn.

sec12-R07-card.front: Do high seats and big mirrors eliminate truck blind spots, and what does the manual call those blind areas?
sec12-R07-card.expected_back: A truck’s elevated seat and large mirrors do not eliminate its broad blind areas, called the NO ZONE.

sec12-R08-card.front: What can happen to your car if you camp inside a truck's blind spot when a hazard appears ahead?
sec12-R08-card.expected_back: Stay out of truck blind spots; an unseen vehicle could be struck if the truck swerves around a hazard.

sec12-R09-card.front: How do you use a truck's side mirror to tell whether the driver can see your car?
sec12-R09-card.expected_back: As a general cue, if the truck’s driver is invisible to you in its side mirror, the driver cannot see you.

sec12-R10-card.front: What must you avoid doing with the open space ahead of a truck or RV to make an exit or turn?
sec12-R10-card.expected_back: Do not cut into a truck’s or RV’s forward space to reach an exit or turn.

sec12-R11-card.front: Why should you avoid pacing alongside a large truck or RV in the next lane?
sec12-R11-card.expected_back: Avoid driving alongside a truck or RV because it may need that space to avoid a road hazard.

sec12-R12-card.front: On which side does the handbook direct you to pass trucks and RVs, and how should you finish?
sec12-R12-card.expected_back: The handbook directs passing trucks and RVs on their left, then moving ahead rather than lingering in a blind spot.

sec12-R13-card.front: Why is tailgating right behind a commercial truck especially dangerous?
sec12-R13-card.expected_back: Do not tailgate a truck; its driver may not know you are close behind.

sec12-R14-card.front: How can the sheer size of an approaching truck or RV fool your eyes?
sec12-R14-card.expected_back: A large truck or RV may appear to be traveling slower than its actual speed.

sec13-F01-card.front: What visual acuity score must an applicant meet on New Mexico's pre-license vision test, and are lenses allowed?
sec13-F01-card.expected_back: The staged manual describes a pre-license vision test requiring at least twenty over forty vision in one or both eyes, with corrective lenses allowed.

sec13-F02-card.front: How does peripheral vision assist while looking straight ahead, and what checks supplement it?
sec13-F02-card.expected_back: Peripheral vision helps detect vehicles and hazards beside you while looking ahead; use mirrors and side glances as needed too.

sec13-F03-card.front: Does passing an eye chart guarantee that a driver judges vehicle distance and speed accurately?
sec13-F03-card.expected_back: Clear eyesight alone does not ensure accurate judgments of distance or speed.

sec13-F04-card.front: Which three driving decisions rely heavily on accurate distance and speed judgment?
sec13-F04-card.expected_back: Distance and speed judgment matter when choosing merge or passing gaps and assessing a train before crossing tracks.

sec13-F05-card.front: What does the New Mexico manual advise if night vision or oncoming headlight glare gives you trouble?
sec13-F05-card.expected_back: If night vision or headlight glare is troublesome, the manual advises limiting nighttime driving to necessity and taking extra care.

sec13-F06-card.front: When must you wear glasses or contact lenses that you need for clear driving vision?
sec13-F06-card.expected_back: Wear the glasses or contact lenses you need for driving whenever you drive.

sec13-F07-card.front: Why must you never wear dark glasses or tinted contact lenses when driving at night?
sec13-F07-card.expected_back: Avoid dark glasses and tinted contacts at night because they reduce the light available for vision.

sec13-F08-card.front: Which four mental and visual abilities suffer when you drive fatigued?
sec13-F08-card.expected_back: Fatigue can impair seeing, alertness, decision speed and decision quality.

sec13-F09-card.front: Beyond slower reactions, what emotional shift and worst-case hazard can tiredness trigger at the wheel?
sec13-F09-card.expected_back: Tiredness may increase irritability and can lead to falling asleep at the wheel.

sec13-F10-card.front: How should you schedule sleep and departure timing before setting out on a long drive?
sec13-F10-card.expected_back: Get your usual night’s sleep before a long trip and plan departure for a time when rested.

sec13-F11-card.front: What medication risk does the handbook's fatigue section warn against before traveling?
sec13-F11-card.expected_back: The fatigue guidance flags medicine that causes drowsiness as a trip risk.

sec13-F12-card.front: Why does the handbook recommend eating a light meal rather than a heavy feast before driving?
sec13-F12-card.expected_back: The handbook advises a light pre-trip meal because a large meal can make some people sleepy.

sec13-F13-card.front: How often does the New Mexico manual recommend taking rest stops on a long trip?
sec13-F13-card.expected_back: On a long trip, the source recommends rest stops about hourly or whenever needed and allowing ample time for the trip.

sec13-F14-card.front: What rest-stop refreshers does the manual list, and what separate rule still overrides them?
sec13-F14-card.expected_back: Its rest-break examples include walking, fresh air and coffee, soda or juice; these are presented alongside its separate prohibition on driving sleepy.

sec13-F15-card.front: What must you do when genuinely sleepy instead of hoping willpower keeps you awake?
sec13-F15-card.expected_back: Do not drive while sleepy; stop to sleep rather than relying on the hope of staying awake.

sec13-F16-card.front: How can traveling with a qualified companion solve highway drowsiness?
sec13-F16-card.expected_back: Where possible, another driver can take over while you sleep.

sec13-F17-card.front: How does alcohol attack judgment, including a drinker's awareness of their own limit?
sec13-F17-card.expected_back: Alcohol can impair judgment as well as driving skill, including the ability to recognize when to stop drinking.

sec13-F18-card.front: How does alcohol affect your reflexes, eyesight clarity, and alertness?
sec13-F18-card.expected_back: Alcohol slows reactions and reflexes, impairs clarity of vision and reduces alertness.

sec13-F19-card.front: What happens to speed-distance reads and vehicle control as alcohol concentration climbs?
