sec01-F24-card.question_text: What alcohol- or drug-offense history during the provisional period disqualifies an unrestricted-license upgrade?
sec01-F24-card.teaching_text: Either an adjudicated alcohol or drug finding or an open pending charge freezes graduated progression.

sec01-R01-card.question_text: During which overnight hours does a provisional license normally bar driving on public highways?
sec01-R01-card.teaching_text: Fatigue and impaired traffic peak after midnight, making late-night hours the riskiest window for teens.

sec01-R02-card.question_text: Who riding inside the car lifts the provisional midnight-to-five curfew?
sec01-R02-card.teaching_text: Having a licensed adult twenty-one or older aboard restores supervised oversight during late-night drives.

sec01-R03-card.question_text: What paperwork allows a provisional driver on the road after midnight for family necessity?
sec01-R03-card.teaching_text: Carrying a signed parental statement proves to an officer on a stop that the late errand is authorized.

sec01-R04-card.question_text: What written proof backs provisional nighttime driving for non-emergency medical necessity?
sec01-R04-card.teaching_text: Documenting late-night pharmacy or clinic needs in writing keeps the provisional driver compliant.

sec01-R05-card.question_text: Whose signed statement authorizes a provisional driver to commute between midnight and five for work?
sec01-R05-card.teaching_text: A parent note does not cover job shifts—your employer must sign the work-commute verification.

sec01-R06-card.question_text: Which four adults can sign a statement excusing provisional night travel for school or religious events?
sec01-R06-card.teaching_text: Late tournament buses or youth-group trips qualify when backed by an official or family signature.

sec01-R07-card.question_text: Which urgent health situation excuses provisional driving between midnight and five?
sec01-R07-card.teaching_text: Urgent medical crises override late-night provisional curfews when immediate care is needed.

sec01-R08-card.question_text: Which two validity lengths does the New Mexico handbook list for driver licenses?
sec01-R08-card.teaching_text: New Mexico issues standard credentials in four-year or eight-year terms before renewal comes due.

sec01-R09-card.question_text: When does the handbook's license-renewal window open and close around expiration?
sec01-R09-card.teaching_text: Renewing inside the ninety-day pre-expiration window keeps your credential active without lapse.

sec01-R10-card.question_text: Which two items does the handbook instruct you to bring when renewing your license?
sec01-R10-card.teaching_text: Showing up with only your expiring plastic card stalls the counter visit without a second identity document.

sec01-R11-card.question_text: Which evaluations can MVD require when you renew a driver license?
sec01-R11-card.teaching_text: Eyesight and rule checks verify continued fitness, with behind-the-wheel drives added in special cases.

sec01-R12-card.question_text: What happens to your driving privileges if you are convicted of driving impaired by alcohol or drugs?
sec01-R12-card.teaching_text: Impaired convictions strip away road privileges alongside criminal fines and court penalties.

sec01-R13-card.question_text: How does refusing a police-requested alcohol or drug check affect your ability to drive?
sec01-R13-card.teaching_text: Under implied-consent rules, saying no to an officer's chemical check triggers license loss on its own.

sec01-R14-card.question_text: What license consequence can follow leaving an involved crash without identifying yourself?
sec01-R14-card.teaching_text: Driving off from a collision without giving your identity turns an accident into a privilege-losing offense.

sec01-R15-card.question_text: What can happen to your license if you put false information on a driver-license application?
sec01-R15-card.teaching_text: Falsifying age, identity, or record details on MVD forms invalidates and revokes your privilege.

sec01-R16-card.question_text: How can failing to settle a court judgment for motor-vehicle crash damages affect you?
sec01-R16-card.teaching_text: Ignoring court-ordered financial damages from a wreck puts your state driving privilege in jeopardy.

sec01-R17-card.question_text: How do altering your license or using someone else's card to buy alcohol affect your driving status?
sec01-R17-card.teaching_text: Using a doctored or borrowed card at a store can cost your legal ability to drive.

sec01-R18-card.question_text: What happens if MVD orders a driver reexamination and you fail to show up?
sec01-R18-card.teaching_text: Ignoring an official MVD retesting notice puts your active credential directly at risk of suspension.

sec01-R19-card.question_text: What privilege penalty applies to using a vehicle in a felony or causing a fatal crash?
sec01-R19-card.teaching_text: Felony vehicle crimes and fatal collisions trigger severe administrative revocation of driving rights.

sec01-R20-card.question_text: What happens when too many violation points stack up on your driving record?
sec01-R20-card.teaching_text: Repeated moving tickets stack up record points until the state suspends your driving license.

sec01-R21-card.question_text: What risk do you run if you let another person use your driver license?
sec01-R21-card.teaching_text: Loaning out your plastic ID penalizes your own driving record right alongside the borrower.

sec01-R22-card.question_text: What restraint check must happen before putting the vehicle in motion?
sec01-R22-card.teaching_text: Confirming belts and child seats before shifting out of park protects everyone from driveway to highway.

sec01-R23-card.question_text: What should you do with the vehicle doors before setting off?
sec01-R23-card.teaching_text: Locked latches help keep doors from popping open during a side impact or rollover.

sec01-R24-card.question_text: How does wearing a safety belt change crash outcomes?
sec01-R24-card.teaching_text: Restraints keep occupants inside the protective cabin shell and away from dashboard or windshield strikes.

sec01-R25-card.question_text: How does New Mexico law treat driving without wearing a safety belt?
sec01-R25-card.teaching_text: Skipping your seat belt is an immediate statutory traffic violation across New Mexico.

sec01-R26-card.question_text: How must a two-part safety belt be worn to deliver full crash protection?
sec01-R26-card.teaching_text: Tucking the shoulder strap behind your back throws your upper torso forward in a frontal hit.

sec01-R27-card.question_text: What manual step is still mandatory in an older car with motorized automatic shoulder belts?
sec01-R27-card.teaching_text: Riding with an automatic chest strap alone lets your hips submarine out under the belt during impact.

sec01-R28-card.question_text: Up to what child age does the New Mexico handbook require appropriate restraints whenever moving?
sec01-R28-card.teaching_text: Every child under twelve needs age-appropriate restraint protection whenever wheels are rolling.

sec01-R29-card.question_text: Which age or weight thresholds require an approved child safety device in the handbook?
sec01-R29-card.teaching_text: Adult seat belts misfit toddlers and light kids, so either under two years or under sixty pounds triggers a safety seat.
sec01-R29-card.must_match_memory_hook: Under twenty-four months or sixty pounds

visual_sync.text_span: Under twenty-four months or sixty pounds

sec01-R30-card.question_text: Where inside the vehicle does the handbook recommend securing children?
sec01-R30-card.teaching_text: Back-row seating puts maximum crush space between young riders and frontal collisions.

sec01-R31-card.question_text: Where does the handbook warn caregivers never to secure a child, and why is it extra dangerous?
sec01-R31-card.teaching_text: Passenger airbags deploy with explosive speed calibrated for adults, causing severe injury to front-row children.

sec01-R32-card.question_text: What option may help a caregiver who cannot afford an approved child safety seat?
sec01-R32-card.teaching_text: Community loaner programs help families ride legally and safely regardless of budget.

sec02-F01-card.question_text: Which three roadway features make up standard forms of traffic control?
sec02-F01-card.teaching_text: Overhead lamps, vertical posts, and lane stripes work together as one coordinated system guiding traffic.

sec02-F02-card.question_text: Which three authorized groups must you obey when they direct traffic in person?
sec02-F02-card.teaching_text: Live hand directions from officers, work flaggers, or school guards override regular lights and posts.

sec02-F03-card.question_text: Under what condition does a green traffic light allow you to proceed?
sec02-F03-card.teaching_text: Green never grants blind immunity if a stalled truck or late walker still occupies the box.

sec02-F04-card.question_text: How are red, yellow, and green positioned on a standard vertical traffic light?
sec02-F04-card.teaching_text: Standardized vertical lamp order lets color-blind drivers read every intersection signal phase reliably.
sec02-F04-card.must_match_memory_hook: Red top, yellow middle, green bottom

visual_sync.text_span: Red top, yellow middle, green bottom

sec02-F05-card.question_text: What legal duty stays active even as you enter an intersection on a steady green light?
sec02-F05-card.teaching_text: Entering on green still requires yielding to oncoming traffic on unprotected lefts and crossing walkers.

sec02-F06-card.question_text: Before rolling forward when your red light turns green, what must happen inside the intersection?
sec02-F06-card.teaching_text: Accelerating into vehicles or walkers finishing the prior phase causes preventable fresh-green collisions.

sec02-F07-card.question_text: What movement does a lighted green arrow authorize?
sec02-F07-card.teaching_text: A green arrow clears your turn movement in the pointed direction while conflicting movements hold.

sec02-F08-card.question_text: Who holds priority when you want to turn left on a circular steady green light?
sec02-F08-card.teaching_text: Unlike a green left arrow, a solid green ball gives oncoming straight-through drivers full priority.

sec02-F09-card.question_text: What should you scan for on posts or mast arms before turning left on a green light?
sec02-F09-card.teaching_text: Busy urban corridors often ban left turns during rush hours or altogether despite a green ball.

sec02-F10-card.question_text: Who must you watch for across your path during both right turns and left turns?
sec02-F10-card.teaching_text: Parallel walk phases release pedestrians straight across the side street you are turning into.

sec02-F11-card.question_text: What does a steady yellow traffic light warn of, and what action does it require?
sec02-F11-card.teaching_text: Gunning the gas to beat yellow risks entering on red, so stop smoothly whenever distance allows.

sec02-F12-card.question_text: What should you do if the signal switches to yellow after you are already inside the intersection?
sec02-F12-card.teaching_text: Slamming to a halt or reversing inside the box traps your car across perpendicular lanes.

sec02-F13-card.question_text: How must you adjust your driving at a flashing yellow traffic light?
sec02-F13-card.teaching_text: Flashing yellow flags high-conflict corners or firehouse aprons without requiring a full stop.

sec02-F14-card.question_text: What phase is ending when a yellow arrow lights up, and how must a turning driver respond?
sec02-F14-card.teaching_text: Once protected arrow time expires, you must either stop safely or yield to oncoming traffic.

sec02-F15-card.question_text: What action is mandatory at a steady circular red traffic light?
sec02-F15-card.teaching_text: Every steady red phase requires a full stop before any permitted turn or green release.

sec02-F16-card.question_text: What does a bright blinking strobe inside a steady red lens mean?
sec02-F16-card.teaching_text: High-visibility strobes grab driver attention on fast highways so nobody overlooks the red stop command.

sec02-R01-card.question_text: After halting for a red light, when may you drive straight ahead?
sec02-R01-card.teaching_text: Straight-through movements never get red-light turn privileges and must wait for a clear green.

sec02-R02-card.question_text: Which three conditions must all be met before turning right on a steady red light?
sec02-R02-card.teaching_text: Rolling the corner or ignoring a No Turn On Red post turns a legal option into a ticket.

sec02-R03-card.question_text: While preparing a permitted right turn on red, whom must you watch for directly ahead?
sec02-R03-card.teaching_text: Drivers craning left for cross-street gaps frequently roll forward into walkers in the front crosswalk.

sec02-R04-card.question_text: Which roadside control matches the exact rule of a flashing red traffic signal?
sec02-R04-card.teaching_text: Treating flashing red like flashing yellow causes broadside crashes—you must halt completely and yield.

sec02-R05-card.question_text: What two commands does a steady red arrow enforce while illuminated?
sec02-R05-card.teaching_text: Unlike a circular red ball, a lighted red arrow bans turning in its pointed direction completely.

sec02-R06-card.question_text: What change at the signal head allows you to move after waiting at a red arrow?
sec02-R06-card.teaching_text: Wait until the red arrow extinguishes and either a green arrow or circular green illuminates.

sec04-F01-card.question_text: Besides separating traffic lanes, what three movements do pavement lines and symbols regulate?
sec04-F01-card.teaching_text: Painted lines work alongside roadside signs so you always know whether crossing lanes or turning is legal right now.

sec04-F02-card.question_text: What two critical intersection zones can pavement markings designate for drivers and walkers?
sec04-F02-card.teaching_text: Painted transverse bars show exactly where walkers cross and where your front bumper must halt for red lights.

sec04-F03-card.question_text: What does a continuous line painted along the side of a roadway identify?
sec04-F03-card.teaching_text: Tracking the outer edge stripe keeps your tires safely on pavement through dark nights, heavy rain, or oncoming glare.

sec04-F04-card.question_text: What is true about the direction of traffic on both sides of white lane lines?
sec04-F04-card.teaching_text: Seeing white dashes beside your door confirms adjacent lanes flow forward with you rather than head-on toward you.

sec04-F05-card.question_text: When does a broken white lane line permit you to move into the next lane?
sec04-F05-card.teaching_text: Dashed paint gives legal permission, yet mirrors, signals, and blind-spot checks decide whether the space is open.

sec04-F06-card.question_text: What does a solid white lane line tell you about changing lanes?
sec04-F06-card.teaching_text: Solid white paint discourages weaving near intersections, tunnels, and exit gores unless an unusual hazard forces a move.

sec04-F07-card.question_text: Where must your vehicle come to rest when a sign or traffic signal requires a stop?
sec04-F07-card.teaching_text: Stopping short of painted bars keeps walkers safe and leaves turning space open for large cross-street vehicles.

sec04-F08-card.question_text: What specific roadway function does a crosswalk identify?
sec04-F08-card.teaching_text: Every marked crossing concentrates foot traffic into a predictable zone where approaching drivers must scan curbs early.

sec04-F09-card.question_text: Which pedestrians at a crosswalk hold right-of-way over approaching vehicles?
sec04-F09-card.teaching_text: Waiting until someone steps off the curb is too late if they are already poised to enter the crossing.

sec04-F10-card.question_text: Do painted white stripes have to be present for a legal pedestrian crossing to exist?
sec04-F10-card.teaching_text: Street intersections create legal unmarked crosswalks between sidewalks, so drivers owe walkers full priority even without paint.

sec04-F11-card.question_text: What kind of traffic flow do yellow lane lines divide?
sec04-F11-card.teaching_text: Keeping yellow paint on your left ensures you never drift into lanes carrying oncoming vehicles head-on.

sec04-F12-card.question_text: When are you allowed to overtake across a single broken yellow center line?
sec04-F12-card.teaching_text: Even on a dashed two-lane stretch, you need clear sight distance and zero oncoming traffic before pulling out.

sec04-F13-card.question_text: What is the passing rule when a solid yellow line sits next to your lane alongside a broken yellow line?
sec04-F13-card.teaching_text: Engineers paint the solid stripe on your side wherever hills or curves block safe passing sightlines ahead.

sec04-F14-card.question_text: When paired solid and broken yellow center lines divide the road, what may a driver beside the broken line do?
sec04-F14-card.teaching_text: Having dashes next to your lane means sightlines open up ahead, provided oncoming traffic leaves a safe gap.

sec04-F15-card.question_text: What passing rule applies when a double solid yellow line runs down the center of the road?
sec04-F15-card.teaching_text: Two solid yellow stripes seal off overtaking for both directions because neither side has safe forward visibility.

sec04-F16-card.question_text: When is turning left across a solid yellow stripe into a private entrance allowed?
sec04-F16-card.teaching_text: Solid yellow stripes forbid overtaking slower cars, not making cautious left turns into private entrances once oncoming traffic clears.

sec04-R14-card.question_text: Which maneuvers are permitted from a shared center lane, and which directions of traffic may enter it?
sec04-R14-card.teaching_text: Using a two-way center lane as a through or passing lane invites head-on crashes with opposing left-turners.

sec04-R15-card.question_text: What pavement symbols show the allowed movements inside a shared middle turn lane?
sec04-R15-card.teaching_text: Opposing curved arrows painted along the middle lane remind drivers that oncoming cars share the exact same turning space.

sec04-R16-card.question_text: How are both outer edges of a shared middle turn lane painted?
sec04-R16-card.teaching_text: Pairing solid outside stripes with dashed inside stripes marks a two-way turn refuge rather than an overtaking lane.

sec04-R01-card.question_text: How does traffic direction work inside a reversible lane?
sec04-R01-card.teaching_text: Cities flip middle lanes between morning inbound rush and evening outbound rush to relieve heavy commuter bottlenecks.

sec04-R02-card.question_text: What yellow pavement markings commonly border a reversible lane?
sec04-R02-card.teaching_text: Double dashed yellow borders warn drivers immediately that travel direction flips by schedule and overhead lane signals.

sec04-R03-card.question_text: What must you check before steering into any reversible lane?
sec04-R03-card.teaching_text: Guessing rush-hour schedules by memory can put you nose-to-nose against oncoming traffic if the lane already flipped.

sec04-R04-card.question_text: What does a green arrow shining directly above a traffic lane mean?
sec04-R04-card.teaching_text: A downward green arrow confirms traffic in your direction owns that reversible lane right now.

sec04-R05-card.question_text: What does a red X displayed above a lane command drivers to do?
sec04-R05-card.teaching_text: Lanes marked with an overhead red cross are closed to your direction and often carry oncoming vehicles.

sec04-R06-card.question_text: How may you use a lane when a flashing yellow X shines overhead?
sec04-R06-card.teaching_text: During off-peak hours an overhead flashing yellow cross converts a reversible lane into a shared left-turn lane only.

sec04-R07-card.question_text: What does a steady yellow X above your lane warn, and what action must you take?
sec04-R07-card.teaching_text: A solid yellow cross announces an imminent flip to a red X, so signal and vacate that lane promptly.

sec04-R08-card.question_text: How do roadways identify a lane set aside for special vehicles or uses?
sec04-R08-card.teaching_text: Spotting a painted white diamond and accompanying rule sign keeps solo drivers out of restricted transit or carpool lanes.

sec04-R09-card.question_text: Which vehicles are allowed to travel in a lane marked Transit or Bus?
sec04-R09-card.teaching_text: Staying clear of dedicated bus corridors avoids hefty fines and keeps public transit schedules moving smoothly.

sec04-R10-card.question_text: Who is a roadway lane labeled Bicycle reserved for?
sec04-R10-card.teaching_text: Cruising or parking inside marked bike lanes forces riders out into fast motor traffic where side-swipe crashes happen.

sec04-R11-card.question_text: What does H O V stand for, and what basic requirement defines an H O V lane?
sec04-R11-card.teaching_text: Carpool lanes reward ridesharing by reserving faster pavement for vehicles carrying more than a lone driver.

sec04-R12-card.question_text: What three pieces of rule information appear on an H O V lane sign?
sec04-R12-card.teaching_text: Checking the schedule plaque tells solo motorists whether carpool restrictions are active right now or open off-peak.

sec04-R13-card.question_text: How many people must be inside your vehicle when a lane posts an H O V three sign?
sec04-R13-card.teaching_text: Busy corridors raise the carpool count to three or more riders, and two-person vehicles can still get ticketed.

sec04-R17-card.question_text: Why must you double-check controls before entering a shared middle lane during peak traffic periods?
sec04-R17-card.teaching_text: A center turn lane you used at noon may carry solid rush-hour through traffic at five, making blind entry dangerous.

sec04-R18-card.question_text: What governs which lane you should use when no specific lane-use signs or markings are present?
sec04-R18-card.teaching_text: Even on unpainted streets, standard rules like keeping right and turning from the nearest curb or center apply.

sec05-F01-card.question_text: Under what lone exception is backing inside a New Mexico travel lane permitted?
sec05-F01-card.teaching_text: Reversing down an active lane surprises approaching traffic and is legal solely for slotting into curb stalls.

sec05-F02-card.question_text: What should you do right after missing your street turn or highway exit?
sec05-F02-card.teaching_text: Driving to the next legal turnaround beats risking a high-speed crash by stopping or reversing.

sec05-F03-card.question_text: How should you handle confusion, car trouble, or letting a passenger out instead of halting in-lane?
sec05-F03-card.teaching_text: Stopping inside a live traffic lane turns minor errands or map checks into rear-end traps.

sec05-F04-card.question_text: Which lane should you use on a road with two or more same-direction lanes?
sec05-F04-card.teaching_text: Staying right on multilane corridors leaves the left lane open for smoother overtaking.

sec05-F05-card.question_text: Which lane should you pick on a three-or-more-lane road with heavy entering and exiting traffic?
sec05-F05-card.teaching_text: Riding the middle lane avoids right-side ramp conflicts while keeping the left passing lane clear.

sec05-F06-card.question_text: When are you allowed to drive along a roadway shoulder?
sec05-F06-card.teaching_text: Shoulders shelter disabled vehicles and responders unless police or road crews wave traffic there.

sec05-F07-card.question_text: What is the intended purpose of the far-left lane on a multilane roadway?
sec05-F07-card.teaching_text: Camping slowly on the far left blocks passing flow and triggers risky right-side weaving.

sec05-F08-card.question_text: What visibility danger arises whenever you overtake another vehicle on its right side?
sec05-F08-card.teaching_text: Passenger-side blind spots are larger, so the other driver may drift right straight into you.

sec05-F09-card.question_text: Does paving a road shoulder make it legal to use for overtaking?
sec05-F09-card.teaching_text: Passing off the main lane edge is illegal regardless of whether the shoulder has asphalt or gravel.

sec05-F10-card.question_text: From which lane do you start and into which lane do you finish an unmarked turn?
sec05-F10-card.teaching_text: Matching closest starting and ending lanes keeps opposing right and left turners from colliding mid-corner.

sec05-F11-card.question_text: What path should your wheels follow between lanes while turning?
sec05-F11-card.teaching_text: Holding a clean, direct arc prevents drifting across adjacent stripes into neighboring traffic.

sec05-F12-card.question_text: When should you move into a different lane if your destination sits beyond the nearest turn lane?
sec05-F12-card.teaching_text: Completing the turn cleanly first lets you recheck mirrors and signal a separate safe shift.

sec05-F13-card.question_text: How often must you use your turn signals for turns and lane changes?
sec05-F13-card.teaching_text: Skipping blinkers on quiet streets misses unseen cyclists, pedestrians, or blind-spot cars.

sec05-F14-card.question_text: What steering habit must you avoid right before making a right turn?
sec05-F14-card.teaching_text: Passenger cars turn tightly without needing tractor-trailer swings into adjacent left lanes.

sec05-R01-card.question_text: How can swinging left before a right turn trap a driver following behind you?
sec05-R01-card.teaching_text: Swinging left mimics a left turn, inviting trailing cars into the exact right gap you cut across.

sec05-R02-card.question_text: Why is drifting out into a farther lane while finishing a right turn hazardous?
sec05-R02-card.teaching_text: Through traffic or opposing left-turners legally holding outer lanes never expect a wide right swing.

sec05-R03-card.question_text: What crash risk comes from slicing across the corner too early during a left turn?
sec05-R03-card.teaching_text: Cutting inside the cross-street center stripe puts your hood head-on into waiting left-side cars.

sec05-R04-card.question_text: Where must you leave room for an oncoming driver who is also turning left?
sec05-R04-card.teaching_text: Turning cleanly in front of each other keeps sightlines open past both windshields.

sec05-R05-card.question_text: What lane rule governs intersections where signs or paint establish multiple turning lanes?
sec05-R05-card.teaching_text: Drifting across dotted guide arcs mid-corner sideswipes the car turning right beside your door.

sec06-F01-card.question_text: What do right-of-way rules clarify when vehicles or pedestrians meet without traffic controls?
sec06-F01-card.teaching_text: Without clear yielding order at unmarked crossings, drivers guess simultaneously and collide right in the conflict zone.

sec06-F02-card.question_text: Does New Mexico law grant an absolute right to go, or does it assign a different responsibility?
sec06-F02-card.teaching_text: Permit questions love testing that nobody ever owns the road, because forcing priority causes preventable wrecks.

sec06-F03-card.question_text: How far must you go to avoid striking a pedestrian or another vehicle in any situation?
sec06-F03-card.teaching_text: Even when another road user makes a mistake, stubbornly holding your path puts lives and liability on you.

sec06-F04-card.question_text: What must you do when a pedestrian steps out while disobeying a traffic control?
sec06-F04-card.teaching_text: A green signal never gives permission to strike someone on foot who misjudged or ignored the walk display.

sec06-F05-card.question_text: Who gets priority when your car crosses a sidewalk to enter or exit a driveway, alley, or lot?
sec06-F05-card.teaching_text: Walkers along a building line can appear suddenly beside parked cars or walls right across your bumper.

sec06-F06-card.question_text: When may your vehicle legally touch a sidewalk, and what sidewalk movement is banned?
sec06-F06-card.teaching_text: Using pedestrian walkways as a shortcut around traffic puts walkers in immediate danger where cars never belong.

sec06-F07-card.question_text: Whose access to roads and sidewalks does the New Mexico White Cane Law protect?
sec06-F07-card.teaching_text: Guaranteed safe passage ensures visually impaired and physically disabled neighbors can travel public streets independently.

sec06-F08-card.question_text: Which New Mexico statute number does the handbook cite for the White Cane Law?
sec06-F08-card.teaching_text: Test writers occasionally pull exact statutory citations straight from the pedestrian safety section to check careful reading.

sec06-F09-card.question_text: What must you do when approaching a blind or partially blind pedestrian with a white or metallic cane or guide dog?
sec06-F09-card.teaching_text: Whether a white or metallic cane has a red tip or not, full caution keeps a vulnerable walker safe.

sec06-F10-card.question_text: What legal consequence hits a driver who skips injury-prevention precautions for a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog?
sec06-F10-card.teaching_text: Failing to protect a walker using a guide dog or white cane creates direct financial liability for any harm caused.

sec06-F11-card.question_text: Who must yield when you want to turn left across oncoming vehicles continuing straight?
sec06-F11-card.teaching_text: Cutting across opposing lanes too early causes severe angle impacts because oncoming traffic holds higher closing speed.

sec06-F12-card.question_text: Who has priority before you pull into a traffic circle or rotary?
sec06-F12-card.teaching_text: Forcing your nose into moving rotary flow disrupts the entire circle and triggers sideswipe crashes.

sec06-F13-card.question_text: Which vehicle gets priority at an intersection with no stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal?
sec06-F13-card.teaching_text: Hesitating or charging through unmarked neighborhood corners leads to side-impact collisions when drivers forget directional priority.

sec06-F14-card.question_text: When vehicles reach a four-way stop at different times, who proceeds first and after what action?
sec06-F14-card.teaching_text: Rolling the limit line to beat another driver breaks intersection rhythm and invites a contested-entry crash.

sec06-F15-card.question_text: Who goes first when two vehicles stop at a four-way intersection at the exact same moment?
sec06-F15-card.teaching_text: Using the right-hand tiebreaker eliminates awkward wave-through standoffs where both cars suddenly lurch forward together.

sec06-F16-card.question_text: Who must yield when pulling onto a street from a driveway, alley, or roadside?
sec06-F16-card.teaching_text: Main-road traffic moves much faster than a departing car, leaving oncoming drivers almost no distance to brake.

sec06-F17-card.question_text: When backed-up traffic fills the far side of an intersection, where must you wait?
sec06-F17-card.teaching_text: Pulling halfway across on green traps your car broadside across cross-street lanes once signals change.

sec06-R01-card.question_text: What yielding rule applies when you overtake a vehicle traveling in the same direction, even if it slows or stops?
sec06-R01-card.teaching_text: A slowing car ahead might be waiting for a hidden turn or walker, making impatient passing around it dangerous.

sec06-R02-card.question_text: Which active audible or visual signals require you to yield to an emergency vehicle?
sec06-R02-card.teaching_text: Seconds matter during fire, medical, and police responses, so any active siren, air horn, or red or blue flash demands space.

sec06-R03-card.question_text: Where should you position your car when an active emergency vehicle approaches from any direction?
sec06-R03-card.teaching_text: Predictably clearing toward the right curb opens a clean center lane so responders never have to weave around stalled cars.

sec06-R04-card.question_text: What must you do if an emergency crew broadcasts directions over a vehicle loudspeaker?
sec06-R04-card.teaching_text: Responders can see crash scenes or blocked lanes ahead that require custom positioning beyond a standard pull-over.

sec06-R05-card.question_text: What should you do first if an active emergency vehicle approaches while you are already inside an intersection?
sec06-R05-card.teaching_text: Stopping dead in the middle of cross streets chokes off every turning path an ambulance or fire truck needs.

sec06-R06-card.question_text: When must you stop for a stopped school bus flashing red lights, and what is the sole oncoming exception?
sec06-R06-card.teaching_text: Students cross unpredictably from both curbs, and only a raised median or physical divider separates oncoming lanes safely.

sec06-R07-card.question_text: When are oncoming drivers exempt from stopping for a school bus with flashing red lights?
sec06-R07-card.teaching_text: Exam questions contrast painted center turn lanes with true medians or physical barriers that actually block children from crossing.

sec06-R08-card.question_text: Once a school bus turns off its flashing red lights, how long must you still remain stopped?
sec06-R08-card.teaching_text: A child dropping papers or doubling back near the bumper stays in danger even after the warning lamps go dark.

sec06-R09-card.question_text: Between road vehicles and a train crossing the roadway, who always yields?
sec06-R09-card.teaching_text: Locomotives weigh thousands of tons and cannot swerve or stop quickly, making any attempt to beat one fatal.

sec06-R10-card.question_text: What must the state post whenever it designates a public road for one-way traffic?
sec06-R10-card.teaching_text: Clear directional signs prevent unfamiliar drivers from accidentally turning head-on into opposing lanes.

sec06-R11-card.question_text: How must you travel once you are on a signed one-way road?
sec06-R11-card.teaching_text: Even backing or cutting a short block against one-way arrows puts you nose-to-nose with drivers expecting clear lanes.

sec06-R12-card.question_text: Which side of the central island must you stay on while driving around a traffic circle or rotary?
sec06-R12-card.teaching_text: Staying to the right of the center island keeps every vehicle flowing counterclockwise without head-on conflicts.

sec08-F01-card.question_text: Why is reading a driver manual alone not enough to learn safe driving?
sec08-F01-card.teaching_text: Muscle memory for timing gaps, braking smoothly, and reading traffic only forms through supervised instruction behind the wheel.

sec08-F02-card.question_text: Which guide should you check for your specific vehicle's proper starting procedure?
sec08-F02-card.teaching_text: Push-button ignitions, cold-start steps, and safety interlocks vary across models, so manufacturer instructions prevent starter damage.

sec08-F03-card.question_text: What brake check must you confirm before starting the engine?
sec08-F03-card.teaching_text: Keeping the car anchored while cranking prevents an unexpected lurch if a gear interlock ever slips.

sec08-F04-card.question_text: What gear state must a manual-transmission vehicle be in before starting?
sec08-F04-card.teaching_text: Cranking a stick-shift while still engaged in gear can make the car jump forward into a wall or bumper.

sec08-F05-card.question_text: What extra pedal step do some manual-transmission vehicles require before the starter engages?
sec08-F05-card.teaching_text: Modern clutch safety switches block ignition cranking until your left foot disconnects the engine from the wheels.

sec08-F06-card.question_text: Which gear position should you select before starting an automatic-transmission vehicle?
sec08-F06-card.teaching_text: Starting in Park locks the output shaft so the car stays planted until your foot is ready on the brake.

sec08-F07-card.question_text: How should you build speed when pulling away instead of stomping the gas?
sec08-F07-card.teaching_text: Progressive throttle keeps weight balanced over all four tires and gives nearby drivers time to read your movement.

sec08-F08-card.question_text: What happens to your driving wheels if you make a sudden start, especially on a slick road?
sec08-F08-card.teaching_text: Breaking tire grip off the line sends the car sliding out of its lane before you even build forward momentum.

sec08-F09-card.question_text: Which two pedals must you practice coordinating on a manual car to prevent stalling or over-revving?
sec08-F09-card.teaching_text: Stalling mid-intersection leaves you stranded across cross traffic, while racing the engine jerks the drivetrain.

sec08-F10-card.question_text: How should your hands grip the steering wheel during normal driving?
sec08-F10-card.teaching_text: One-handed cruising leaves you unable to counter a sudden pothole, crosswind gust, or tire blowout.

sec08-F11-card.question_text: Which primary clock-face hand position does the staged New Mexico handbook present as a balanced grip?
sec08-F11-card.teaching_text: New Mexico permit questions still reference the handbook's stated clock-face positions alongside modern alternatives.

sec08-F12-card.question_text: Which second clock-face hand position does the handbook describe as an alternative balanced grip?
sec08-F12-card.teaching_text: Holding wide at nine and three gives strong leverage across the wheel while keeping arms clear of the center hub.

sec08-F13-card.question_text: Where should your knuckles stay relative to the steering-wheel rim?
sec08-F13-card.teaching_text: Hooking thumbs or knuckles inside the spokes risks broken fingers if a curb strike spins the wheel violently.

sec08-F14-card.question_text: Where should you aim your eyes so you spot upcoming steering adjustments early?
sec08-F14-card.teaching_text: Staring right over your hood hides curves and shoulder hazards until only jerky corrections remain.

sec08-F15-card.question_text: Which steering technique does the handbook describe for turning around a sharp corner?
sec08-F15-card.teaching_text: Smooth hand-over-hand pulls deliver quick, controlled steering angle without losing a solid grip on the rim.

sec08-F16-card.question_text: How should you bring the steering wheel back to straight after finishing a turn?
sec08-F16-card.teaching_text: Actively feeding the rim back straight keeps the front tires pointed precisely down your new lane.

sec08-F17-card.question_text: Why should you avoid letting the steering wheel spin freely back through your fingers?
sec08-F17-card.teaching_text: Unchecked self-centering can overshoot straight ahead or snag a finger right as traffic closes around you.

sec08-F18-card.question_text: Why must you glance at your speedometer frequently instead of trusting how fast the car feels?
sec08-F18-card.teaching_text: Quiet cabins and smooth pavement mask rising velocity until you are carrying far too much pace into a hazard.

sec08-F19-card.question_text: What speed-judgment error commonly traps drivers right after exiting a fast highway onto a slower local street?
sec08-F19-card.teaching_text: After miles at freeway pace, forty-five feels like crawling even though you are speeding past neighborhood driveways.

sec08-F20-card.question_text: What straightforward rule applies to posted speed-limit signs along your route?
sec08-F20-card.teaching_text: Engineers set each zone's ceiling around sightlines, curves, and side access you may not spot at first glance.

sec08-F21-card.question_text: How should you time your search for stopping situations ahead?
sec08-F21-card.teaching_text: Catching brake lights or stale greens early lets you ease off the gas instead of slamming the pedal.

sec08-F22-card.question_text: What vehicle-control danger can abrupt braking trigger?
sec08-F22-card.teaching_text: Locking or overloading tires in a panic stomp strips away steering control right when you need it most.

sec08-F23-card.question_text: How does a sudden stop affect drivers traveling behind your vehicle?
sec08-F23-card.teaching_text: Slamming on the brakes shrinks the following driver's stopping margin to nearly zero, inviting a chain-reaction crash.

sec08-F24-card.question_text: What smoother options replace a panic stop when you recognize road hazards early?
sec08-F24-card.teaching_text: Extra time lets you blend gently into an open lane or bleed off speed without startling surrounding cars.

sec08-F25-card.question_text: Which directions around your car must you continuously scan to stay aware of traffic events?
sec08-F25-card.teaching_text: Tunnel vision straight ahead misses merging cars on your flanks and tailgaters closing fast in your mirrors.

sec08-F26-card.question_text: How does active scanning protect you from people or vehicles near your travel lane?
sec08-F26-card.teaching_text: Noticing turned front wheels or a walker stepping off a curb early gives you space to adjust smoothly.

sec08-F27-card.question_text: Besides people and vehicles, what crucial roadside information does steady scanning uncover?
sec08-F27-card.teaching_text: Catching curve warnings and exit signs early prevents frantic last-second lane dives across solid lines.

sec08-F28-card.question_text: How does looking well ahead change your steering and braking inputs?
sec08-F28-card.teaching_text: Drivers who read the road early rarely have to yank the wheel or stab the brake pedal.

sec08-F29-card.question_text: What two everyday benefits come from looking well ahead besides crash prevention?
sec08-F29-card.teaching_text: Coasting early instead of accelerating into red lights burns less gas and smooths stop-and-go waves behind you.

sec08-F30-card.question_text: How does far-ahead scanning improve the way your car tracks inside its lane?
sec08-F30-card.teaching_text: Your hands naturally steer toward your eyes, so aiming high down the lane centers the car effortlessly.

sec08-F31-card.question_text: At least how many seconds ahead does the New Mexico handbook say safer drivers tend to look?
sec08-F31-card.teaching_text: Exam questions test exact eye-lead numbers by state, and New Mexico sets ten seconds as its baseline.

sec08-F32-card.question_text: In city traffic, roughly what physical distance equals the handbook's ten-second look-ahead?
sec08-F32-card.teaching_text: Visualizing one full city block makes a ten-second scan easy to judge without counting nonstop in traffic.

sec08-F33-card.question_text: How far ahead does the handbook recommend scanning while driving in the city?
sec08-F33-card.teaching_text: Watching the next signal and crosswalk a block up keeps double-parked delivery vans from catching you off guard.

sec08-F34-card.question_text: Where is looking toward both sides for entering vehicles or walkers especially critical?
sec08-F34-card.teaching_text: Crossings where roads or rails intersect your lane carry the highest risk of high-energy side impacts.

sec08-F35-card.question_text: What broad range of locations counts as an intersection according to the handbook?
sec08-F35-card.teaching_text: Treating shopping-lot aprons and residential driveways like real intersections keeps pull-out surprises on your radar.

sec08-F36-card.question_text: Which directions must you check for traffic and pedestrians before entering any intersection?
sec08-F36-card.teaching_text: Cross-street cars from the left reach your lane first, while runners or cyclists can step off either curb.

sec08-F37-card.question_text: After making a full stop at an intersection, what must you do right before accelerating?
sec08-F37-card.teaching_text: A fast motorcycle or jogger can move into your blind pillar gap during the second your car sits stopped.

sec08-F38-card.question_text: What must you verify about your entire crossing path before rolling into an intersection?
sec08-F38-card.teaching_text: Getting trapped mid-box behind backed-up bumpers blocks cross traffic and invites T-bone collisions.

sec08-F39-card.question_text: What visibility check is mandatory before committing your vehicle into an intersection?
sec08-F39-card.teaching_text: Pulling out blind past hedges, walls, or parked vans gambles your side doors on luck alone.

sec08-R01-card.question_text: What must you wait for before turning left across approaching traffic?
sec08-R01-card.teaching_text: Misjudging oncoming speed forces incoming drivers to slam their brakes while your passenger side sits exposed.

sec08-R02-card.question_text: Why must you scan the destination street before starting a left turn across oncoming lanes?
sec08-R02-card.teaching_text: A walker or backed-up bumper in the side street can freeze your turn broadside across oncoming traffic.

sec08-R03-card.question_text: Where should your eyes look one final time immediately before turning left across oncoming traffic?
sec08-R03-card.teaching_text: A hidden car whipping out from behind a turning truck can close your gap in the last split second.

sec08-R04-card.question_text: Which approaching traffic stream must you check before turning right?
sec08-R04-card.teaching_text: Vehicles coming from your left share the exact curb lane you are about to pull into.

sec08-R05-card.question_text: What oncoming-vehicle movement must you watch for before turning right?
sec08-R05-card.teaching_text: An opposing driver turning left on a green arrow or misjudging lane width can swing straight into your lane.

sec08-R06-card.question_text: Where must you check for pedestrians before starting a right turn?
sec08-R06-card.teaching_text: Drivers staring left for a car gap often roll right into pedestrians stepping into the side-street crosswalk.

sec08-R07-card.question_text: When is New Mexico's general permission to turn right on a red light canceled?
sec08-R07-card.teaching_text: Blind corners and heavy pedestrian crossings post explicit bans where red-light turns create unacceptable crash rates.

sec08-R08-card.question_text: When does the handbook permit turning left from one one-way street onto another one-way street?
sec08-R08-card.teaching_text: Exam traps contrast legal one-way-to-one-way left turns against illegal red-light lefts involving any two-way street.

sec08-R09-card.question_text: Why must you never assume a stop sign or red signal guarantees cross traffic will stop?
sec08-R09-card.teaching_text: Paint and bulbs cannot physically brake a distracted or impaired driver barreling toward your door.

sec08-R10-card.question_text: Should you still look left and right when cross traffic faces a stop sign or red light?
sec08-R10-card.teaching_text: Two quick head checks spot red-light runners before your front end enters their collision line.

sec08-R11-card.question_text: Why is extra caution needed right after your traffic signal turns green?
sec08-R11-card.teaching_text: Launching instantly on a fresh green puts you straight into cross-street drivers trying to beat their red.

sec08-R12-card.question_text: How should you proceed after stopping if hedges, walls, or parked vehicles block your cross-street view?
sec08-R12-card.teaching_text: Inching ahead keeps your stopping distance tiny until your eyes clear the obstruction.

sec08-R13-card.question_text: How does edging forward slowly help cross-street drivers when a corner view is obstructed?
sec08-R13-card.teaching_text: Seeing your bumper inch out early gives cross traffic time to ease off the gas or tap a warning horn.

sec08-R14-card.question_text: Which roadside environments demand extra scanning because people may step suddenly into the street?
sec08-R14-card.teaching_text: Crowded sidewalks, lots, playgrounds, and road-work zones keep people focused on errands or tasks rather than traffic.

sec08-R15-card.question_text: What two actions must you take at every railroad crossing approach?
sec08-R15-card.teaching_text: Warning gates or bulbs can malfunction, so only easing speed and scanning both tracks confirms clear rails.

sec08-R16-card.question_text: How should you treat a familiar railroad crossing where you have never seen a train?
sec08-R16-card.teaching_text: Freight and maintenance trains run unscheduled hours, turning complacency on quiet local spurs into fatal surprises.

sec08-R17-card.question_text: What space check must pass before you start driving across railroad tracks?
sec08-R17-card.teaching_text: Stopping with your tail hanging over the rails leaves zero escape if gates drop behind you.

sec08-R18-card.question_text: Why must you wait until a passing train moves well down the line at a multitrack crossing?
sec08-R18-card.teaching_text: A second locomotive racing opposite on the adjacent track stays completely hidden behind the caboose until impact.

sec08-R19-card.question_text: How should your mirror-checking pace change when traffic volume turns heavy?
sec08-R19-card.teaching_text: Dense traffic packs shrink following gaps fast, so frequent mirror glances keep tailgaters from surprising you.

sec08-R20-card.question_text: What two dangerous following behaviors do regular rear checks reveal?
sec08-R20-card.teaching_text: Catching a bumper riding too close or closing fast lets you widen your front cushion early.

sec08-R21-card.question_text: Before which four maneuvers or road features are rear-traffic checks especially important?
sec08-R21-card.teaching_text: Lane changes, slowdowns, backing, and steep descents all alter your spacing with drivers directly behind you.

sec08-R22-card.question_text: Which two zones must you check for vehicles in the target lane before changing lanes?
sec08-R22-card.teaching_text: A car already beside you or closing fast from behind will occupy that exact space mid-move.

sec08-R23-card.question_text: Besides moving between marked travel lanes, what two entries count as lane changes?
sec08-R23-card.teaching_text: Merging off an entrance ramp or pulling out from a shoulder requires the exact same mirror-and-shoulder checks.

sec08-R24-card.question_text: Which mirrors should you use together to check whether your target lane is clear?
sec08-R24-card.teaching_text: Pairing interior and exterior mirrors shows both distance behind and lateral offset before your head check.

sec08-R25-card.question_text: What passing conflict must you rule out before drifting into an adjacent lane?
sec08-R25-card.teaching_text: Pulling out in front of an accelerating passer leaves them nowhere to go at closing highway speeds.

sec08-R26-card.question_text: How do you check the spaces near your car's rear corners before moving sideways?
sec08-R26-card.teaching_text: Turning your chin toward the target lane sweeps the exact rear-quarter pocket where compact cars and bikes hide.

sec08-R27-card.question_text: What name describes the rear-corner zones around your car that mirrors cannot show?
sec08-R27-card.teaching_text: Even well-aimed glass leaves rear-corner pockets invisible without a direct over-the-shoulder glance.

sec08-R28-card.question_text: Why must your side and rear checks stay brief?
sec08-R28-card.teaching_text: Staring backward for two full seconds can put you straight into brake lights that flared ahead while you turned.

sec08-R29-card.question_text: Why should you use mirrors first while preparing to merge, change lanes, or enter traffic?
sec08-R29-card.teaching_text: Quick mirror flicks let you size up gaps early without taking your eyes off lead traffic for long.

sec08-R30-card.question_text: When should you perform your over-the-shoulder blind-spot check for a lane change?
sec08-R30-card.teaching_text: A car can slip into your rear quarter between your mirror glance and steering input unless checked last.

sec08-R31-card.question_text: Which is safer when checking away from the road ahead, one long stare or several quick looks?
sec08-R31-card.teaching_text: Splitting checks into short snapshots refreshes your forward view between glances so sudden stops never ambush you.

sec08-R32-card.question_text: Which two traffic streams must you keep tracking while actually changing lanes?
sec08-R32-card.teaching_text: Either your old lead car or your new lane's lead car can brake mid-merge.

sec08-R33-card.question_text: On a road with three or more lanes, why must you check the lane beyond your target lane?
sec08-R33-card.teaching_text: Two drivers converging into the same middle pocket from opposite sides collide instantly if neither looks two lanes over.

sec08-R34-card.question_text: Which three groups of road users are harder to spot than cars or trucks?
sec08-R34-card.teaching_text: Narrow silhouettes slip behind windshield pillars, mirrors, and parked roofs where a quick car-sized glance misses them.

sec08-R35-card.question_text: When must you be extra alert for cyclists, motorcyclists, and walkers along the road edge?
sec08-R35-card.teaching_text: Bikes and walkers hug the exact curb line you cross when pulling out from a driveway or parked stall.

sec08-R36-card.question_text: When should slowing down trigger an immediate rear-traffic check, and when is that check most critical?
sec08-R36-card.teaching_text: Braking abruptly for a late driveway or open parking spot catches following drivers completely unprepared.

sec08-R37-card.question_text: Why should you keep backing movements to a minimum?
sec08-R37-card.teaching_text: High trunk lids and pillars hide huge low zones directly behind your rear bumper.

sec08-R38-card.question_text: How can smart stall choice in a parking lot eliminate backing out later?
sec08-R38-card.teaching_text: Leaving forward gives you full windshield sightlines of shopping carts, kids, and aisle traffic.

sec08-R39-card.question_text: What should you inspect behind your parked car before climbing in to back up?
sec08-R39-card.teaching_text: Toddlers, pets, and low toys sit completely below rear glass once you settle into the driver's seat.

sec08-R40-card.question_text: What body position does the handbook describe for looking rearward while backing?
sec08-R40-card.teaching_text: Pivoting your torso to look directly out the back window opens a far wider view than glancing sideways.

sec08-R41-card.question_text: Why must you never rely solely on mirrors while backing up?
sec08-R41-card.teaching_text: Side and interior glass leave a dead zone straight behind the tailpipe where pedestrians can stand unseen.

sec08-R42-card.question_text: Why must you keep your speed very slow whenever reversing?
sec08-R42-card.teaching_text: Front wheels swing the nose wide in reverse, so fast backing amplifies tiny steering errors into curb or fender hits.

sec08-R43-card.question_text: Who should you ask for help during a tricky backing movement whenever available?
sec08-R43-card.teaching_text: A helper standing clear beside the path can see low curbs and cross traffic hidden from the cabin.

sec08-R44-card.question_text: What should you watch for in your mirrors during a long or steep downhill descent?
sec08-R44-card.teaching_text: Gravity builds speed fast on mountain grades, and spotting a fast closer early lets you clear the right lane.

sec08-R45-card.question_text: Which specific vehicles behind you demand extra downhill alertness if they approach too fast?
sec08-R45-card.teaching_text: Heavy rigs or buses suffering overheated brakes on New Mexico mountain passes cannot slow down easily behind you.

sec11-F01-card.question_text: What safety advantage do you gain by keeping more space between your vehicle and other road users?
sec11-F01-card.teaching_text: Extra separation gives your eyes and feet critical seconds to steer or brake smoothly instead of panicking.

sec11-F02-card.question_text: What crash type commonly results from following too closely when the vehicle ahead brakes suddenly?
sec11-F02-card.teaching_text: Human reaction lag guarantees your bumper is still flying forward while the leading car is already stopping.

sec11-F03-card.question_text: How do you use a fixed roadside object to measure the three-second following gap?
sec11-F03-card.teaching_text: Fixed signs or shadows give an objective time check because eyeballing highway footage misleads almost every driver.

sec11-F04-card.question_text: What does it mean if your front bumper reaches the roadside marker before you finish counting three seconds?
sec11-F04-card.teaching_text: Finishing the count late proves your stopping margin is shorter than highway brake-reaction physics demands.

sec11-F05-card.question_text: How should you correct your position after failing a three-second following check?
sec11-F05-card.teaching_text: Rechecking at the next signpost confirms you actually opened a real time cushion rather than easing off briefly.

sec11-F06-card.question_text: How many seconds of following gap does the New Mexico manual suggest on slippery pavement or behind a motorcycle?
sec11-F06-card.teaching_text: Wet asphalt stretches your braking distance while lightweight two-wheelers can shed speed or swerve abruptly.

sec11-F07-card.question_text: What following interval does the manual list as an example when pulling a heavy trailer or trailing an emergency vehicle?
sec11-F07-card.teaching_text: Towed weight pushes your vehicle forward under braking while emergency rigs may turn or halt unpredictably.

sec11-F08-card.question_text: Which two roadway or grade situations also appear in the handbook's four-second following-space examples?
sec11-F08-card.teaching_text: Buses stop unexpectedly at tracks and manual-shift vehicles can roll backward slightly when launching uphill.

sec11-F09-card.question_text: What two habits help a driver behind you maintain a safe following cushion?
sec11-F09-card.teaching_text: Predictable throttle and early brake or turn warnings prevent chain-reaction surprises behind your rear bumper.

sec11-F10-card.question_text: Why should you keep open space beside your vehicle on both sides whenever traffic allows?
sec11-F10-card.teaching_text: Boxing yourself tightly between neighboring cars leaves nowhere to steer when sudden debris appears ahead.

sec11-F11-card.question_text: How should you position your car on a road with two or more lanes when traffic is entering?
sec11-F11-card.teaching_text: Sliding left into an open lane eliminates ramp bottlenecks and side-by-side merge conflicts.

sec11-F12-card.question_text: How should you adjust your lane position when driving past a line of parked cars?
sec11-F12-card.teaching_text: One flung car door or pedestrian stepping from between bumpers happens faster than brakes can react.

sec11-F13-card.question_text: Who deserves extra side clearance along the roadway, and which age group needs special vigilance?
sec11-F13-card.teaching_text: Children dart without checking traffic, turning tight curb passes into tragic Split-second emergencies.

sec11-F14-card.question_text: Roughly how many seconds of traffic gap does the New Mexico handbook specify for merging?
sec11-F14-card.teaching_text: Squeezing into tiny gaps forces both you and trailing traffic onto the brakes mid-lane.

sec11-F15-card.question_text: When you pull squarely into the middle of a four-second traffic gap, what buffers remain ahead and behind?
sec11-F15-card.teaching_text: Splitting the opening evenly gives both you and the trailing driver breathing room while cushions widen.

sec11-F16-card.question_text: To which three everyday traffic movements does the handbook apply its four-second merge gap?
sec11-F16-card.teaching_text: Whether shifting lanes, pulling onto a highway, or blending tapers, identical closing-speed math applies.

sec11-F17-card.question_text: What rule applies when the opening beside you is smaller than a safe merging gap?
sec11-F17-card.teaching_text: Assuming another motorist will slam brakes to let your fender in triggers high-speed sideswipes.

sec11-F18-card.question_text: How must you move across a multi-lane roadway when shifting over several lanes?
sec11-F18-card.teaching_text: Sweeping diagonally across three lanes blindsides drivers merging into that same middle lane from the opposite side.

sec11-F19-card.question_text: How big must a traffic gap be before you drive straight across an intersecting roadway?
sec11-F19-card.teaching_text: Getting stranded halfway across leaves your side doors sitting squarely inside high-speed through lanes.

sec11-F20-card.question_text: Beyond room for the turn itself, what else must your gap allow when turning into moving traffic?
sec11-F20-card.teaching_text: Pulling out slowly forces fast approaching traffic to swerve or lock brakes behind your bumper.

sec11-F21-card.question_text: Before starting a left turn, what two potential blockers must be clear of your target path?
sec11-F21-card.teaching_text: Watching only oncoming headlights often leaves turning cars stopped sideways for walkers in the far crosswalk.

sec11-F22-card.question_text: Does a green traffic light allow you to pull into an intersection when backed-up cars block the far side?
sec11-F22-card.teaching_text: Getting stranded inside the box when signals cycle gridlocks cross-traffic and emergency responders.

sec11-F23-card.question_text: When is it legal and safe to drive onto a railroad crossing behind slow traffic?
sec11-F23-card.teaching_text: Stopping on steel tracks behind a red-light line leaves nowhere to go if crossing bells start ringing.

sec11-R01-card.question_text: Do dashed centerlines or passing-zone signs guarantee that overtaking right now is safe?
sec11-R01-card.teaching_text: Rain, glare, or fast oncoming traffic can make a marked passing zone lethal in real time.

sec11-R02-card.question_text: How many vehicles should you overtake in a single pass as a general rule?
sec11-R02-card.teaching_text: Leapfrogging a long line of cars doubles exposure time in the oncoming lane and risks losing your return gap.

sec11-R03-card.question_text: At fifty-five miles per hour, roughly how long does a pass take according to the New Mexico handbook?
sec11-R03-card.teaching_text: Two cars closing toward each other at highway pace eat up nearly a third of a mile in ten seconds.

sec11-R04-card.question_text: How far ahead must your view stay clear when passing near hills or curves?
sec11-R04-card.teaching_text: Starting a pass with less clear road ahead gambles your life that the blind crest is empty.

sec11-R05-card.question_text: What must you always assume whenever a hill crest or curve blocks your forward view?
sec11-R05-card.teaching_text: Defensive drivers treat every blind curve as occupied until clear pavement proves otherwise.

sec11-R06-card.question_text: Within what distance of an approaching hill or curve must you never start a pass?
sec11-R06-card.teaching_text: Exam questions test this exact distance because highway closing speeds leave zero time to abort near crests.

sec11-R07-card.question_text: Why is passing hazardous near intersections, railroad tracks, and shopping-center driveways?
sec11-R07-card.teaching_text: Pulling into the opposing lane right where cars or trains cross creates blind angle collisions.

sec11-R08-card.question_text: What three major hazards can the vehicle you are overtaking hide from your sight?
sec11-R08-card.teaching_text: A slowing van ahead might be yielding for a pedestrian or train that your left-lane pass never sees.

sec11-R09-card.question_text: How can a side-street driver turning right create a sudden threat while you pass in the opposing lane?
sec11-R09-card.teaching_text: Drivers turning right out of driveways look left for gaps and pull straight nose-to-nose into passing cars.

sec11-R10-card.question_text: What roadside situations should you scan for before overtaking in case another vehicle swerves sideways?
sec11-R10-card.teaching_text: A parked delivery van or pothole ahead can make the car you are passing juke straight into your door.

sec11-R11-card.question_text: How do pedestrians or cyclists along the road edge affect your ability to overtake?
sec11-R11-card.teaching_text: The lead driver will naturally drift left to clear walkers or bikes, pinching off your passing lane.

sec11-R12-card.question_text: Which structure widths or pavement flaws can wipe out safe room to pass?
sec11-R12-card.teaching_text: Hitting black ice or pinched bridge rails mid-pass strips away both traction and lateral escape space.

sec11-R13-card.question_text: What must already exist ahead of the vehicle you overtake before you pull out to pass?
sec11-R13-card.teaching_text: Counting on tight platoons of cars to brake and open a slot leaves you trapped facing oncoming headlights.

sec11-R14-card.question_text: What is the rule on overtaking when a railroad grade crossing lies ahead?
sec11-R14-card.teaching_text: Gates dropping or lead cars braking for tracks can trap a passing car on the wrong side.

sec11-R15-card.question_text: What visual check in your rearview mirror confirms safe clearance to pull back into the right lane after passing?
sec11-R15-card.teaching_text: Cutting back before spotting the entire grille clips fenders or steals the passed driver's braking cushion.

sec12-F01-card.question_text: How do a bicyclist's legal rights and duties on New Mexico roads compare with a car driver's?
sec12-F01-card.teaching_text: Recognizing bicycles as lawful traffic operators prevents impatient cutoffs at four-way stops and turn lanes.

sec12-F02-card.question_text: How much lateral clearance does the New Mexico handbook tell drivers to aim for when overtaking a cyclist?
sec12-F02-card.teaching_text: Notice New Mexico specifies a generous five-foot target so mirror gusts and road bumps never clip handlebars.

sec12-F03-card.question_text: How should you respond when a cyclist ahead signals to merge across or enter a turn lane?
sec12-F03-card.teaching_text: Pedal power accelerates slower than engines, so easing off lets riders position safely without getting boxed curb-side.

sec12-F04-card.question_text: What piece of lawful equipment does the handbook compare a bicycle to when sharing traffic lanes?
sec12-F04-card.teaching_text: Framing a bike like slow work machinery reminds impatient motorists to wait calmly for a legal passing zone.

sec12-F05-card.question_text: Even though cyclists normally ride right, what lane position may they legally take when needed?
sec12-F05-card.teaching_text: Honking at a centered rider ignores that New Mexico law explicitly protects full-lane positioning for safety.

sec12-F06-card.question_text: What three everyday situations justify a bicyclist riding down the middle of the full lane?
sec12-F06-card.teaching_text: Drainage grates, broken glass, and pinched curbs leave center-lane riding as the only upright line.

sec12-F07-card.question_text: How must you execute a right turn when a bicyclist is riding alongside on your right?
sec12-F07-card.teaching_text: Racing ahead to chop right across a moving front wheel causes classic broadside right-hook crashes.

sec12-F08-card.question_text: Which group of cyclists is especially likely to make unexpected lane shifts or sudden turns?
sec12-F08-card.teaching_text: Young riders focus on pedaling rather than shoulder checks, swerving abruptly without hand signals.

sec12-F09-card.question_text: How do stop signs, red lights, and traffic laws apply to bicyclists on the road?
sec12-F09-card.teaching_text: Predictable compliance with signals and lane rules keeps bikes and cars reading intersections identically.

sec12-F10-card.question_text: What front and rear visibility equipment does the New Mexico handbook require on a bicycle at night?
sec12-F10-card.teaching_text: Unlit dark bicycles disappear completely against asphalt shadows until headlights are dangerously close.

sec12-F11-card.question_text: In what direction must cyclists ride, and how should they execute intersection turns?
sec12-F11-card.teaching_text: Riding against oncoming cars puts cyclists in blind angles where cross-street drivers never look.

sec12-F13-card.question_text: What three practical habits help a cyclist stay noticeable to motorists?

sec12-F14-card.question_text: Which riding direction does the New Mexico manual identify as the safest position for a bicycle in traffic?
sec12-F14-card.teaching_text: Moving in the same direction lowers relative closing speed and places riders inside drivers' normal forward scan.

sec12-F15-card.question_text: How does the New Mexico handbook's helmet guidance differ between adult riders and minors?
sec12-F15-card.teaching_text: Permit questions separate strong safety recommendations for adults from mandatory helmet compliance under eighteen.

sec12-F16-card.question_text: What do sharrow pavement markings designate on a street?
sec12-F16-card.teaching_text: Unlike exclusive bike lanes set off by solid stripes, sharrows mark one lane shared sequentially by cars and bikes.

sec12-F17-card.question_text: On what kind of street width are sharrows painted?
sec12-F17-card.teaching_text: Cities stamp sharrows specifically where squeezing past inside the same lane would brush handlebars or mirrors.

sec12-F18-card.question_text: What does a sharrow encourage bicyclists to do, and what does it require from drivers?
sec12-F18-card.teaching_text: Sharrows legally validate center-lane cycling while reminding trailing drivers to wait patiently behind.

sec12-F19-card.question_text: How should you adjust your driving when catching up to a cyclist on a sharrow-marked street?
sec12-F19-card.teaching_text: Tailgating or revving behind an unprotected rider in a narrow shared lane creates rear-end danger.

sec12-F20-card.question_text: When may a motorist overtake a cyclist along a route with sharrows?
sec12-F20-card.teaching_text: Holding back until the corridor widens keeps both vehicles separated safely without curb-pinching.

sec12-F21-card.question_text: How much passing clearance does the handbook's sharrow guidance ask motorists to aim for?
sec12-F21-card.teaching_text: Matching the five-foot clearance rule ensures passing never crowds a rider against gutters or parked bumpers.

sec12-F22-card.question_text: Where on the painted sharrow symbol is a bicyclist allowed to ride?
sec12-F22-card.teaching_text: Engineers paint the chevron center specifically outside the parked-car door zone to guide safe tire tracking.

sec12-F23-card.question_text: What curbside hazard zone does the sharrow section warn bicyclists to stay clear of?
sec12-F23-card.teaching_text: Riding an arm's length clear of parked fenders prevents getting clotheslined into moving traffic.

sec12-F24-card.question_text: When should a cyclist move toward the right to let trailing traffic pass?
sec12-F24-card.teaching_text: Cyclists never have to duck into gravel or parked-door gaps until wide clean pavement makes moving right safe.

sec12-R01-card.question_text: How does stopping distance for a large truck or RV compare with a passenger car at identical speed?
sec12-R01-card.teaching_text: Multi-ton campers and freight rigs carry massive kinetic energy that stretches every highway brake zone.

sec12-R02-card.question_text: In the New Mexico handbook's fifty-five-mile-per-hour example, compare stopping distance for an average car versus a large truck?
sec12-R02-card.teaching_text: Notice New Mexico's manual cites roughly double the footage for heavy rigs, making cut-ins catastrophic.
