sec12-R03-card.question_text: Why must you never pull in front of a heavy truck and suddenly slow down or stop?
sec12-R03-card.teaching_text: Stealing a truck's forward braking cushion leaves tens of thousands of pounds nowhere to go except through your trunk.

sec12-R04-card.question_text: How do large trucks and RVs handle tight corners, especially right turns?
sec12-R04-card.teaching_text: Long wheelbases track sharply inside corners, requiring wide setups so rear duals clear the curb.

sec12-R05-card.question_text: What must you inspect on a large vehicle ahead before starting to overtake it?
sec12-R05-card.teaching_text: Verifying blinkers first prevents diving alongside a long rig right as it starts a wide turn.

sec12-R06-card.question_text: If a truck ahead drifts left as if turning left, why must you wait and recheck its blinkers?
sec12-R06-card.teaching_text: Squeezing down the right curb past a left-swinging tractor puts you directly inside the folding trailer path.

sec12-R07-card.question_text: Do high seats and big mirrors eliminate truck blind spots, and what does the manual call those blind areas?
sec12-R07-card.teaching_text: Knowing the No-Zone label helps test-takers spot blind-area questions around all four sides of commercial rigs.

sec12-R08-card.question_text: What can happen to your car if you camp inside a truck's blind spot when a hazard appears ahead?
sec12-R08-card.teaching_text: A trucker dodging blown tire treads cannot avoid a passenger car hidden silently beside the trailer.

sec12-R09-card.question_text: How do you use a truck's side mirror to tell whether the driver can see your car?
sec12-R09-card.teaching_text: Dropping back until you spot the trucker's face in the glass guarantees mutual line of sight.

sec12-R10-card.question_text: What must you avoid doing with the open space ahead of a truck or RV to make an exit or turn?
sec12-R10-card.teaching_text: Slotting behind a big rig to catch your ramp beats risking a high-speed clip across its front bumper.

sec12-R11-card.question_text: Why should you avoid pacing alongside a large truck or RV in the next lane?
sec12-R11-card.teaching_text: Keeping adjacent lanes open gives heavy vehicles lateral room around stalled cars or wind gusts.

sec12-R12-card.question_text: On which side does the handbook direct you to pass trucks and RVs, and how should you finish?
sec12-R12-card.teaching_text: Left-side blind zones are smaller than right-side ones, and brisk completion clears the No-Zone fast.

sec12-R13-card.question_text: Why is tailgating right behind a commercial truck especially dangerous?
sec12-R13-card.teaching_text: Tucked behind solid trailer doors, you lose forward sight while the trucker has zero idea you are there.

sec12-R14-card.question_text: How can the sheer size of an approaching truck or RV fool your eyes?
sec12-R14-card.teaching_text: Optical scale makes big vehicles appear leisurely right up until they arrive at highway speed.

sec13-F01-card.question_text: What visual acuity score must an applicant meet on New Mexico's pre-license vision test, and are lenses allowed?
sec13-F01-card.teaching_text: Screening eyesight before licensing ensures every driver can read regulatory signs early enough to react safely.

sec13-F02-card.question_text: How does peripheral vision assist while looking straight ahead, and what checks supplement it?
sec13-F02-card.teaching_text: Outer vision catches movement early while mirror sweeps and shoulder glances supply sharp detail.

sec13-F03-card.question_text: Does passing an eye chart guarantee that a driver judges vehicle distance and speed accurately?
sec13-F03-card.teaching_text: Crisp letter reading does not automatically gauge how fast oncoming headlights are closing a two-lane gap.

sec13-F04-card.question_text: Which three driving decisions rely heavily on accurate distance and speed judgment?
sec13-F04-card.teaching_text: Misjudging closing speed at highway ramps, two-lane passes, or rail crossings leaves zero room for error.

sec13-F05-card.question_text: What does the New Mexico manual advise if night vision or oncoming headlight glare gives you trouble?
sec13-F05-card.teaching_text: Shifting optional errands into daylight hours avoids glare fatigue when dark contrast drops.

sec13-F06-card.question_text: When must you wear glasses or contact lenses that you need for clear driving vision?
sec13-F06-card.teaching_text: Skipping prescription frames even on short neighborhood errands blurs crosswalks and bike lanes.

sec13-F07-card.question_text: Why must you never wear dark glasses or tinted contact lenses when driving at night?
sec13-F07-card.teaching_text: Dimming low-beam illumination further hides dark pedestrians, wandering animals, and unpainted curb edges.

sec13-F08-card.question_text: Which four mental and visual abilities suffer when you drive fatigued?
sec13-F08-card.teaching_text: Exhaustion degrades both how fast you notice brake lights and whether you choose the right response.

sec13-F09-card.question_text: Beyond slower reactions, what emotional shift and worst-case hazard can tiredness trigger at the wheel?
sec13-F09-card.teaching_text: Short-tempered highway frustration often precedes nodding off completely across a live lane.

sec13-F10-card.question_text: How should you schedule sleep and departure timing before setting out on a long drive?
sec13-F10-card.teaching_text: Leaving right after a full workday guarantees nighttime fatigue hits before you reach half distance.

sec13-F11-card.question_text: What medication risk does the handbook's fatigue section warn against before traveling?
sec13-F11-card.teaching_text: Allergy or cold tablets compound highway monotony and pull eyelids shut miles from town.

sec13-F12-card.question_text: Why does the handbook recommend eating a light meal rather than a heavy feast before driving?
sec13-F12-card.teaching_text: Digesting huge portions saps afternoon alertness right when steady highway concentration matters most.

sec13-F13-card.question_text: How often does the New Mexico manual recommend taking rest stops on a long trip?
sec13-F13-card.teaching_text: Frequent short stretch stops prevent deep fatigue from building up in the first place.

sec13-F14-card.question_text: What rest-stop refreshers does the manual list, and what separate rule still overrides them?
sec13-F14-card.teaching_text: A brisk walk and coffee refresh alert travelers, yet genuine sleepiness still demands real sleep.

sec13-F15-card.question_text: What must you do when genuinely sleepy instead of hoping willpower keeps you awake?
sec13-F15-card.teaching_text: Willpower cannot override brain chemistry once microsleeps start shutting your eyes for seconds at highway speed.

sec13-F16-card.question_text: How can traveling with a qualified companion solve highway drowsiness?
sec13-F16-card.teaching_text: Trading seats lets a fresh driver watch the road while you get genuine rest.

sec13-F17-card.question_text: How does alcohol attack judgment, including a drinker's awareness of their own limit?
sec13-F17-card.teaching_text: Because alcohol numbs self-assessment early, buzzed people lose the ability to tell they had too much.

sec13-F18-card.question_text: How does alcohol affect your reflexes, eyesight clarity, and alertness?
sec13-F18-card.teaching_text: Delayed foot movement plus fuzzy nighttime focus stretches stopping distances well past safe margins.

sec13-F19-card.question_text: What happens to speed-distance reads and vehicle control as alcohol concentration climbs?
sec13-F19-card.teaching_text: Higher blood alcohol warps how fast cross-traffic looks while making steering inputs sloppy and late.

sec13-F20-card.question_text: How many alcoholic drinks does it take to begin affecting your driving?
sec13-F20-card.teaching_text: Measurable declines in divided attention and hazard scanning begin well below legal arrest limits.

sec13-F21-card.question_text: What serving sizes of eighty-proof liquor, beer, and wine count as one equivalent drink in the manual?
sec13-F21-card.teaching_text: Exam questions test standard-drink equivalents because beer and wine carry the exact same alcohol load per serving.

sec13-F22-card.question_text: Why can counting one glass as one drink mislead you with specialty cocktails?
sec13-F22-card.teaching_text: Tall mixed pours often pack multiple liquor shots into a single sweet glass.

sec13-F23-card.question_text: Do coffee, cold showers, exercise, or fresh air sober someone up, and what actually works?
sec13-F23-card.teaching_text: Stimulants and cold water wake up an impaired person without lowering blood alcohol one bit.

sec13-F24-card.question_text: What three ride options should you arrange when attending an event where alcohol is served?
sec13-F24-card.teaching_text: Deciding how you get home before the first pour removes impaired midnight guesswork.

sec13-F25-card.question_text: How severely can legal prescription or over-the-counter medicines impair your driving?
sec13-F25-card.teaching_text: Assuming a store-bought or doctor-prescribed pill is harmless ignores heavy sedation and slowed steering.

sec13-F26-card.question_text: Which four common categories of everyday medicine can trigger driving drowsiness?
sec13-F26-card.teaching_text: Everyday antihistamines and calming tablets routinely carry sedating ingredients that ambush unsuspecting commuters.

sec13-F27-card.question_text: What dangerous rebound effects follow the brief wakeful feeling from stimulant or diet pills?
sec13-F27-card.teaching_text: Artificial pep wears off abruptly mid-highway, leaving shaky hands and dizzy tunnel vision.

sec13-F28-card.question_text: Where should you look and whom should you ask if unsure whether a medicine affects driving?
sec13-F28-card.teaching_text: Pharmacists and doctors spot sedating interactions in seconds before you ever start the car.

sec13-F29-card.question_text: Why does the handbook warn strictly against mixing alcohol with other drugs or medicines?
sec13-F29-card.teaching_text: One drink paired with a sedating pill can compound impairment several times over and threaten life.

sec13-F30-card.question_text: How does the staged New Mexico manual treat illegal drugs, including marijuana in its example, for driving?
sec13-F30-card.teaching_text: Slowed reaction timing and distorted tracking make drug-impaired driving a major roadway crash threat.

sec13-R01-card.question_text: Below what age does the handbook state buying, consuming, or possessing alcohol is prohibited?
sec13-R01-card.teaching_text: All three acts carry strict underage enforcement before a young person ever reaches legal adulthood.

sec13-R02-card.question_text: At or above what blood alcohol concentration can an adult driver face arrest according to the manual?
sec13-R02-card.teaching_text: Reaching this per-se threshold supports DWI arrest regardless of whether the driver claims to feel steady.

sec13-R03-card.question_text: At what blood alcohol concentration can a driver under twenty-one face arrest according to the handbook?
sec13-R03-card.teaching_text: Zero-tolerance youth thresholds mean even trace alcohol from a single drink triggers arrest.

sec13-R04-card.question_text: What does BAC stand for, and which three body samples does the manual list for testing it?
sec13-R04-card.teaching_text: Chemical testing statutes cover all three sample methods to measure alcohol circulating in the body.

sec13-R05-card.question_text: How long can you lose your license for refusing an officer's requested BAC test according to the manual?

sec13-R06-card.question_text: What financial and custody penalties does the manual list for a first DWI conviction?
sec13-R06-card.teaching_text: Even a first offense brings courtroom expenses and potential incarceration on top of license fallout.

sec13-R07-card.question_text: Beyond fines and possible jail, what two requirements apply on a first New Mexico DWI conviction?

sec13-R08-card.question_text: What licensing action does New Mexico MVD hold authority to take following a DWI?

sec13-R09-card.question_text: Which three penalty categories climb steeper upon second and subsequent DWI convictions?

sec13-R10-card.question_text: How many years does a DWI conviction stay on a New Mexico driving record according to the handbook?
sec13-R10-card.teaching_text: Exam writers love this specific number because a single youthful DWI follows your record for decades.

sec13-R11-card.question_text: Is driving unlawful under the influence of any drug that makes operating a vehicle unsafe?

sec13-F31-card.question_text: How should you handle transportation when a cold, cough, stiff neck, or sore leg impairs your driving?
sec13-F31-card.teaching_text: A stiff neck blocks blind-spot checks while leg pain slows emergency brake transitions.

sec13-R12-card.question_text: Which medical conditions require periodic physician-signed medical statements filed with MVD?
sec13-R12-card.teaching_text: Periodic medical reviews confirm chronic conditions stay controlled well enough to protect everyone on the road.

sec13-R13-card.question_text: Which state agency provides detailed rules and forms for medical-condition driver reporting?

sec13-R14-card.question_text: Along with regular checkups and medicine care, how long must an applicant with epilepsy stay seizure-free before licensing?

sec13-R15-card.question_text: When does the handbook warn a driver with insulin-treated diabetes not to get behind the wheel?
sec13-R15-card.teaching_text: Sudden hypoglycemic blackouts or convulsions leave a moving car completely uncontrolled in live traffic.

sec13-R16-card.question_text: What two everyday slip-ups does the manual note can trigger a dangerous insulin reaction?
sec13-R16-card.teaching_text: Keeping meal timing and insulin dosing matched prevents sudden blood-sugar drops mid-commute.

sec13-R17-card.question_text: What transportation precaution does the manual recommend while a physician is adjusting your insulin dosage?

sec13-R18-card.question_text: Why does the handbook's diabetes section recommend regular eye exams?
sec13-R18-card.teaching_text: Diabetes can quietly degrade retinal health and low-light vision long before daytime sight seems affected.

sec13-R19-card.question_text: Which cardiovascular conditions and sudden-episode risks carry a handbook warning against driving?
sec13-R19-card.teaching_text: Fainting or suffering a cardiac episode at highway speed endangers both the driver and oncoming lanes.

sec13-R20-card.question_text: What specific question should someone under a doctor's care for a heart condition ask at appointments?
sec13-R20-card.teaching_text: Your cardiologist knows whether your symptoms or heart medications could trigger sudden dizziness on the road.

sec13-R21-card.question_text: Which five strong emotional states does the manual warn can interfere with safe driving?
sec13-R21-card.teaching_text: Intense feelings hijack working memory so drivers look right at brake lights without registering them.

sec13-R22-card.question_text: What should you do if you feel heated with anger or overly excited before a trip?
sec13-R22-card.teaching_text: Taking ten minutes parked to cool down prevents aggressive speeding and impulsive lane cuts.

sec13-R23-card.question_text: If you must drive while worried or upset, what mental discipline does the handbook stress?
sec13-R23-card.teaching_text: Consciously anchoring attention onto mirrors, spacing, and signals stops personal stress from drifting your lane.

sec13-R24-card.question_text: What two everyday mobile-phone actions does the manual warn can dangerously distract a driver?
sec13-R24-card.teaching_text: Looking down at digits steals your eyes while phone conversations narrow cognitive hazard scanning.

sec13-R25-card.question_text: Where should you handle making or taking a phone call whenever conditions allow?
sec13-R25-card.teaching_text: Stopping clear of live lanes lets you talk or dial with zero risk of drifting into traffic.

sec13-R26-card.question_text: What local rule does the handbook mention regarding handheld phones in certain municipalities?
sec13-R26-card.teaching_text: Municipal ordinances can ticket handheld calls at city limits even if you never touch a keypad.

sec10-F01-card.question_text: How does higher travel speed change the road space needed to turn, slow down, or stop?
sec10-F01-card.teaching_text: Momentum climbs disproportionately fast with velocity, forcing brakes and tires to eat up far more pavement.

sec10-F02-card.question_text: When must you cut speed for road geometry or wet pavement conditions?
sec10-F02-card.teaching_text: Carrying highway speed into a tight bend or standing water strips cornering traction right when side loads spike.

sec10-F03-card.question_text: Which two paired sets of factors determine how well your tires grip the road?
sec10-F03-card.teaching_text: Even brand-new tread slips on glazed ice, while bald rubber slides easily on damp asphalt.

sec10-F04-card.question_text: How should you maintain your tires, and where do you check the proper inflation pressure?
sec10-F04-card.teaching_text: Sidewall numbers show maximum tire ratings rather than your car's tuned pressure listed inside the owner's manual.

sec10-F05-card.question_text: Why must you drop speed when switching from asphalt or concrete onto dirt or gravel?
sec10-F05-card.teaching_text: Loose stones roll like marbles beneath tires, stretching braking distances and making cornering skids easy.

sec10-F06-card.question_text: When should you finish slowing for a curve, and what happens if you brake mid-curve?
sec10-F06-card.teaching_text: Tires have a fixed traction budget, so demanding heavy braking and cornering together breaks grip.

sec10-F07-card.question_text: What should you do right when rain, snow, or sleet first begins falling?
sec10-F07-card.teaching_text: Traction drops immediately as moisture coats dry pavement, well before puddles or snowbanks pile up.

sec10-F08-card.question_text: By roughly how much does the New Mexico handbook recommend lowering speed on wet pavement?
sec10-F08-card.teaching_text: Shaving about ten miles per hour restores crucial stopping margin when water lubricates asphalt.

sec10-F09-card.question_text: How much does the handbook recommend cutting your speed on packed snow?
sec10-F09-card.teaching_text: Permit exams pair minus ten on wet pavement against half speed on packed snow to test winter judgment.

sec10-F10-card.question_text: What tire equipment does the handbook recommend when snow covers the road?
sec10-F10-card.teaching_text: Standard all-season tread packs full of slush quickly on snow-covered New Mexico mountain passes.

sec10-F11-card.question_text: What two pieces of advice does the handbook give when roads are coated in ice?
sec10-F11-card.teaching_text: Even four-wheel drive cannot shorten braking on glare ice, making postponing the trip the smartest call.

sec10-F12-card.question_text: Why is permission to run studded tires restricted differently depending on the area and road?
sec10-F12-card.teaching_text: Local rules restrict metal studs where bare dry highways would suffer costly rutting and surface wear.

sec10-F13-card.question_text: How do cold, wet shaded patches behave compared with sunlit stretches of pavement?
sec10-F13-card.teaching_text: Canyon walls, trees, and buildings block warming sun, leaving surprise black-ice patches in afternoon shadows.

sec10-F14-card.question_text: Why can bridges and overpasses ice over even while the surrounding highway stays clear?
sec10-F14-card.teaching_text: Cold air chills elevated concrete from both top and bottom while ground heat still warms regular roadbeds.

sec10-F15-card.question_text: How does wet ice near freezing compare with dry ice at bitter subzero temperatures?
sec10-F15-card.teaching_text: A thin film of meltwater sits atop thirty-two-degree ice, acting like liquid bearings under rubber.

sec10-F16-card.question_text: Why are the opening minutes of a hot-weather rainstorm extra slick?
sec10-F16-card.teaching_text: Dripped motor oil and rubber dust float into a greasy film before steady rainfall washes the lane clean.

sec10-F17-card.question_text: Up to roughly what speed do most tires hold good wet-road grip before rising speed starts lifting them onto water?
sec10-F17-card.teaching_text: Above roughly thirty-five miles per hour, tire grooves struggle to channel water fast enough, starting hydroplaning.

sec10-F18-card.question_text: At roughly what speed in heavy rain does the handbook warn tires may lose all road grip?
sec10-F18-card.teaching_text: At fifty miles per hour in downpours, water wedges completely beneath the tread so steering and brakes disconnect.

sec10-F19-card.question_text: How do bald or heavily worn tires change the speed at which wet-road traction disappears?
sec10-F19-card.teaching_text: Shallow tread lacks escape channels for water, floating the tire well below thirty-five miles per hour.

sec10-F20-card.question_text: What is your primary defense for cutting hydroplaning risk in rain or on wet pavement?
sec10-F20-card.teaching_text: Lower speed gives tire grooves enough time to squeeze water out and maintain solid asphalt contact.

sec10-F21-card.question_text: What pedal action should you take first if your tires start losing grip on water?
sec10-F21-card.teaching_text: Lifting smoothly shifts weight gently onto the front tires so they can sink back through the water layer.

sec10-F22-card.question_text: How should you handle the steering wheel after losing traction, and when is turning permitted?
sec10-F22-card.teaching_text: Cranking the wheel while floating leaves front tires cocked sideways, causing a violent spin once grip snaps back.

sec10-F23-card.question_text: What two inputs should you avoid until your tires reconnect with the pavement, aside from a slow emergency steer?
sec10-F23-card.teaching_text: Hitting the brakes on a water wedge locks the wheels and destabilizes the car the instant rubber touches asphalt.

sec10-F24-card.question_text: Even with good tires, good brakes, and dry pavement, roughly how many feet can reacting and stopping from fifty miles per hour take?
sec10-F24-card.teaching_text: Four hundred feet exceeds a full football field, surprising drivers who underestimate reaction plus braking distance.

sec10-F25-card.question_text: Under ideal dry conditions with good tires and brakes, roughly how far can stopping from thirty miles per hour take?
sec10-F25-card.teaching_text: Memorizing two hundred feet at thirty alongside four hundred at fifty nails New Mexico's stopping-distance pairs.

sec10-F26-card.question_text: How do the four-hundred-foot and two-hundred-foot visibility thresholds cap safe travel speeds?
sec10-F26-card.teaching_text: Driving fifty with less than four hundred feet of sight, or thirty under two hundred, outruns your stopping room.

sec10-F27-card.question_text: What rule governs how fast you may travel after dark?
sec10-F27-card.teaching_text: Outrunning your beam throws an unlit animal, stalled truck, or washout into view too late to stop short.

sec10-F28-card.question_text: Roughly how far does the manual estimate headlights illuminate ahead, and what speed example fits stopping within that reach?
sec10-F28-card.teaching_text: Because fifty miles per hour already eats four hundred dry feet to stop, faster dark-highway speeds overrun your beams.

sec10-F29-card.question_text: When heavy rain, a snowstorm, or dense fog cuts sight distance to about two hundred feet, what speed should you not exceed?
sec10-F29-card.teaching_text: With only two hundred feet visible through fog or blizzard conditions, anything past thirty outruns even dry-road braking.

sec10-F30-card.question_text: What should you do when a severe downpour cuts visibility too low to keep driving safely?
sec10-F30-card.teaching_text: Pushing blind through a cloudburst gambles on guessing lane lines while stopped cars hide ahead in spray.

sec10-F31-card.question_text: How should you choose your approach speed for a hillcrest or blind curve?
sec10-F31-card.teaching_text: A stalled car, rockslide, or herd can sit dead still just past the crest or bend.

sec10-F32-card.question_text: How much lateral room should you leave when passing a row of parked vehicles, and why?
sec10-F32-card.teaching_text: Wide lateral space gives you time to react when someone steps between bumpers or swings a door open.

sec10-F33-card.question_text: How do you perform the handbook's four-second sight-distance check?
sec10-F33-card.teaching_text: Timing four full seconds toward a clear stationary landmark measures whether your speed fits current visibility.

sec10-F34-card.question_text: What does reaching your chosen landmark before finishing a four-second count tell you to do?
sec10-F34-card.teaching_text: Arriving under four seconds proves you are outrunning your clear sight zone and need to ease off.

sec10-F35-card.question_text: Why should you run the four-second sight-distance check while driving at night?
sec10-F35-card.teaching_text: Counting four seconds to the edge of your headlight pool confirms you can stop inside illuminated pavement.

sec10-R01-card.question_text: Where should you scan for wildlife, and what should seeing roadkill along the highway prompt you to do?
sec10-R01-card.teaching_text: Struck animals mark established game trails where other herd members still cross the highway regularly.

sec10-R02-card.question_text: Which five large animals does the New Mexico manual highlight as roadway hazards?
sec10-R02-card.teaching_text: Striking mature elk, deer, or bears causes severe cabin intrusion, making rural scanning life-critical across New Mexico.

sec10-R03-card.question_text: Where across New Mexico does the manual place deer, elk, pronghorn antelope, and bears or cougars?
sec10-R03-card.teaching_text: Knowing elk roam the western three-quarters, antelope cross eastern open plains, and bears haunt mountains sharpens regional scanning.

sec10-R04-card.question_text: During which daily light periods must you stay sharpest for animals entering the road?
sec10-R04-card.teaching_text: Game animals feed and move actively right when low twilight glare hides dark coats along highway shoulders.

sec10-R05-card.question_text: Why shouldn't you count on an animal bolting clear, and what should you expect right after one crosses?
sec10-R05-card.teaching_text: Headlights often freeze animals mid-lane, and trailing fawns or herd mates bolt across seconds behind the leader.

sec10-R06-card.question_text: How do hoofed animals move on wet or icy pavement, and how should you respond?
sec10-R06-card.teaching_text: Hard hooves lose traction on slick asphalt, causing deer or elk to stumble and linger across your lane.

sec10-R07-card.question_text: What risk comes from driving faster than surrounding traffic, and what pace adjustment fixes it?
sec10-R07-card.teaching_text: Every extra pass adds another blind-spot exposure and lane-change conflict that matching safe traffic flow avoids.

sec10-R08-card.question_text: What traffic problem does driving far slower than everyone else create, and what should you do if a line forms behind you?
sec10-R08-card.teaching_text: Bunched packs grow impatient and attempt risky two-lane passes unless you pull aside safely to clear them.

sec10-R09-card.question_text: How should you use a highway entrance ramp to prepare for merging?
sec10-R09-card.teaching_text: Joining fast lanes at highway pace lets you slip smoothly into a gap without forcing trucks to slam brakes.

sec10-R10-card.question_text: Why must you avoid driving to the end of an entrance ramp and stopping?
sec10-R10-card.teaching_text: Starting from zero at the merge tip leaves no runway to build speed while ramp followers watch left over their shoulders.

sec10-R11-card.question_text: How should you wait on an entrance ramp if freeway traffic has no immediate opening?
sec10-R11-card.teaching_text: Holding back early on the ramp preserves pavement ahead so you can punch up to freeway speed once a gap opens.

sec10-R12-card.question_text: Where should you hold full traffic speed and where should you start braking when leaving a highway?
sec10-R12-card.teaching_text: Braking early inside main freeway lanes invites high-speed rear-end crashes from drivers behind you.

sec10-R13-card.question_text: How should you handle braking when turning off a fast two-lane highway with traffic behind you?
sec10-R13-card.teaching_text: Crawling way too early frustrates fast followers, while flashing brake taps before a crisp slowdown warns them cleanly.

sec10-R14-card.question_text: Why must you spot slow-moving vehicles well up the road?
sec10-R14-card.teaching_text: Closing on a crawling vehicle at highway pace shrinks gaps astonishingly fast unless you merge or ease off early.

sec10-R15-card.question_text: How do steep uphill grades and roadway merges affect large trucks and low-powered small cars?
sec10-R15-card.teaching_text: Expecting slow climbs and long merge acceleration keeps you from tailgating struggling vehicles on mountain grades.

sec10-R16-card.question_text: What typical top speed and rear marker identify tractors, animal-drawn rigs, and road-maintenance machines?
sec10-R16-card.teaching_text: Spotting that fluorescent orange triangle warns instantly that you are closing on a twenty-five-mile-per-hour vehicle.

sec10-R17-card.question_text: How should your speed change whenever traffic or pedestrians crowd your available maneuvering space?
sec10-R17-card.teaching_text: When side escape lanes vanish, only slower forward pace gives you enough time to brake short.

sec10-R18-card.question_text: Which four everyday high-activity zones often require dropping below normal cruising speeds?
sec10-R18-card.teaching_text: Stop-and-go bumpers, backing shoppers, and jaywalking commuters pack dense conflicts into every yard.

sec10-R19-card.question_text: Why can narrow bridges and tunnels require slowing down?
sec10-R19-card.teaching_text: Zero shoulder room and tight centerline margins leave little forgiveness if an oncoming mirror drifts wide.

sec10-R20-card.question_text: Which four sudden traffic shifts must you anticipate when approaching and leaving a toll plaza?
sec10-R20-card.teaching_text: Drivers fan out across booths and funnel back into fewer lanes while braking and sprinting unpredictably.

sec10-R21-card.question_text: What hazard must stay top of mind near schools, playgrounds, and residential homes?
sec10-R21-card.teaching_text: Children chasing balls or friends focus completely on play and bolt past parked fenders without checking traffic.

sec10-R22-card.question_text: Besides checking for trains and far-side room, why else might you need to slow at a railroad crossing?
sec10-R22-card.teaching_text: Uneven timber or raised steel tracks can jolt suspension or bounce tires off line if hit too fast.

sec03-F01-card.question_text: What five kinds of information do road signs communicate to drivers?
sec03-F01-card.teaching_text: Every posted panel on New Mexico highways fits one core job so drivers can anticipate rules, hazards, or exits early.

sec03-F02-card.question_text: Which two visual features help you recognize the type of message a road sign carries?
sec03-F02-card.teaching_text: Glancing at background color and outer shape lets you classify a sign from far away even in glare or fog.

sec03-F03-card.question_text: What background color, symbol color, and shape do most warning signs use?
sec03-F03-card.teaching_text: Spotting a yellow diamond ahead gives you extra seconds to scan for curves, merges, or crossings before reaching danger.

sec03-F04-card.question_text: How should you respond as soon as you spot a warning sign ahead?
sec03-F04-card.teaching_text: Easing off the gas early keeps stopping distance in reserve if the upcoming hazard blocks your lane unexpectedly.

sec03-F18-card.question_text: What color combination and shapes identify most work-area signs?
sec03-F18-card.teaching_text: Bright orange panels alert you immediately that road crews, shifted lanes, or temporary hazards lie just ahead.

sec03-F19-card.question_text: What four roadway conditions can work-area warning signs alert you to expect?
sec03-F19-card.teaching_text: Construction zones combine heavy machinery with abrupt pavement drops, so anticipating sudden surface or route changes prevents rear-end crashes.

sec03-F20-card.question_text: What must you do when a worker directs traffic with a flag or handheld sign in a work zone?
sec03-F20-card.teaching_text: Crew members hold live sightlines around single-lane closures and heavy equipment, so their directions override normal traffic flow.

sec03-F21-card.question_text: Which five driving requirements do regulatory signs communicate?
sec03-F21-card.teaching_text: Ignoring a regulatory panel is a citable traffic violation because each one states a mandatory legal requirement on the road.

sec03-F22-card.question_text: What three shape categories can regulatory signs take?
sec03-F22-card.teaching_text: Unique outlines like octagons and downward triangles let drivers tell critical right-of-way commands apart even from behind.

sec03-F23-card.question_text: Which background colors and symbol or letter colors commonly appear on regulatory signs?
sec03-F23-card.teaching_text: High-contrast red, white, black, and green markings help drivers distinguish prohibitions from permitted movements at a glance.

sec03-F25-card.question_text: What two kinds of legal speeds can a posted speed-limit sign establish?
sec03-F25-card.teaching_text: Highways sometimes post both top and bottom limits so fast traffic does not slam into dangerously slow vehicles.

sec03-F26-card.question_text: When is driving at the posted maximum speed appropriate, and what do bad conditions require?
sec03-F26-card.teaching_text: Rain, dust, ice, or heavy traffic stretches stopping distance, making the posted top number unsafe and unlawful.

sec03-F05-card.question_text: What does New Mexico law and safety guidance say about trying to beat an approaching train?
sec03-F05-card.teaching_text: Locomotives weigh thousands of tons and cannot swerve or brake quickly, turning any misjudged gap into a fatal impact.

sec03-F06-card.question_text: When is it safe to pull onto a railroad crossing with traffic ahead of you?
sec03-F06-card.teaching_text: Getting boxed onto rails by backed-up traffic leaves nowhere to escape if crossing bells start ringing.

sec03-F07-card.question_text: Why must you avoid shifting gears while your vehicle is crossing railroad tracks?
sec03-F07-card.teaching_text: Missing a shift can stall your engine directly across the rails with an oncoming train closing fast.

sec03-F08-card.question_text: How does a train's huge size affect how fast it looks as it approaches a crossing?
sec03-F08-card.teaching_text: Large objects create a visual illusion of slow motion, tricking impatient drivers into pulling onto active rails.

sec03-F09-card.question_text: What does a circular yellow sign displaying an X and the letters R R warn you to expect?
sec03-F09-card.teaching_text: Spotting the round yellow warning early gives you time to quiet the cabin, scan both ways, and cover the brake.

sec03-F10-card.question_text: What does a white railroad crossbuck mark, and what right-of-way duty does it impose?
sec03-F10-card.teaching_text: Treat every white crossbuck exactly like a yield command where approaching rail traffic always holds absolute priority.

sec03-F11-card.question_text: What must you do when alternating lights begin flashing at a railroad crossing?
sec03-F11-card.teaching_text: Alternating red flashes signal an approaching locomotive, making rolling through the crossing both illegal and deadly.

sec03-F12-card.question_text: What is the strict rule whenever a railroad-crossing gate is lowered across the lane?
sec03-F12-card.teaching_text: Weaving past a dropped arm puts your car directly into the path of a fast-moving train you may not see.

sec03-F13-card.question_text: How long must you wait when a railroad crossing bell or horn is sounding?
sec03-F13-card.teaching_text: Moving before warning bells silence risks colliding with a second train approaching from the opposite direction.

sec03-F14-card.question_text: What specific danger does a sign displaying a number of railroad tracks warn drivers about?
sec03-F14-card.teaching_text: A caboose clearing the nearest rail can hide a second express train charging down the parallel track.

sec03-F15-card.question_text: Why must you look for extra sets of rails even if no multiple-track plaque is posted?
sec03-F15-card.teaching_text: Not every multi-rail crossing carries a supplemental number plaque, so visual verification is your last defense.

sec03-F16-card.question_text: Which vehicles must stop at least fifteen feet before railroad tracks, causing traffic behind them to expect sudden braking?
sec03-F16-card.teaching_text: Following school buses, passenger-carrying for-hire cars, or hazardous-material trucks too closely invites rear-end collisions at every rail line.

sec03-F17-card.question_text: What specific action must a school-bus driver take before driving across railroad tracks?
sec03-F17-card.teaching_text: Opening the doors lets the driver hear train horns or bells clearly over cabin noise before pulling onto rails.

sec03-F27-card.question_text: What exact shape, background color, and black markings appear on the advance railroad warning sign?
sec03-F27-card.teaching_text: Only advance rail warnings use a yellow circle, making them unmistakable from diamond-shaped general hazard panels.

sec03-F28-card.question_text: What color, shape, and exact words identify a standard railroad crossbuck?
sec03-F28-card.teaching_text: Recognizing the white X silhouette right at the rail line tells you immediately where train tracks intersect your road.

sec03-R01-card.question_text: Why does a posted minimum speed sign require you to drive at least as fast as the number shown?
sec03-R01-card.teaching_text: Crawling below the floor speed on a fast highway turns your vehicle into a rolling obstacle for closing traffic.

sec03-R02-card.question_text: What should you do when weather, load, or vehicle condition keeps you below a highway's posted minimum speed?
sec03-R02-card.teaching_text: Switching to a lower-speed route keeps both you and high-speed freeway drivers safe when safe travel requires going slow.

sec03-R03-card.question_text: How do lane-control signs show which turns and movements are allowed from each lane?
sec03-R03-card.teaching_text: Spotting directional arrows early lets you merge smoothly instead of cutting across lanes right at the intersection.

sec03-R04-card.question_text: What roadway marking often works alongside overhead or roadside lane-control signs?
sec03-R04-card.teaching_text: Curved or straight pavement arrows confirm your lane's legal path even when tall trucks block roadside posts.

sec03-R05-card.question_text: Why are no-passing signs posted along certain stretches of two-lane roadway?
sec03-R05-card.teaching_text: Hills, curves, and side roads hide oncoming cars until it is far too late to abort an overtaking pass.

sec03-R06-card.question_text: Does leaving a no-passing zone mean you can pull out to overtake right away?
sec03-R06-card.teaching_text: Signage only marks sightline geometry, so you still have to verify oncoming gaps and traffic before pulling left.

sec03-R07-card.question_text: What exact shape, background color, and letter color identify a stop sign?
sec03-R07-card.teaching_text: Eight-sided geometry belongs exclusively to stop commands so drivers can recognize intersection priority even covered in frost.

sec03-R08-card.question_text: Where must you bring your vehicle to a complete halt at a stop sign with or without a painted line?
sec03-R08-card.teaching_text: Rolling past the painted limit line blocks pedestrian walkways and noses your bumper into cross-traffic lanes.

sec03-R09-card.question_text: Once you make a full stop at a stop sign, when are you allowed to pull forward?
sec03-R09-card.teaching_text: Stopping is only half the legal duty because pulling out into pedestrians or cross vehicles still causes right-of-way crashes.

sec03-R10-card.question_text: What colors and orientation distinguish a standard yield sign?
sec03-R10-card.teaching_text: No other traffic sign points a three-sided tip straight down, letting cross traffic see who must give way.

sec03-R11-card.question_text: How must you adjust speed and right-of-way when approaching a yield sign?
sec03-R11-card.teaching_text: Approaching gently lets you merge smoothly into a safe gap or stop cleanly if vehicles occupy the intersection.

sec03-R12-card.question_text: What does a square sign featuring a white horizontal bar inside a red circle command?
sec03-R12-card.teaching_text: Passing that bold red emblem sends your car head-on against one-way lanes or freeway off-ramp traffic.

sec03-R13-card.question_text: What kind of roadway opening commonly displays Do Not Enter signs?
sec03-R13-card.teaching_text: Highway off-ramps and divided-road crossovers post entry bans so turning drivers never steer into oncoming freeway lanes.

sec03-R14-card.question_text: What maximum travel speed does a reflective orange triangle on the back of a vehicle indicate?
sec03-R14-card.teaching_text: Farm tractors and maintenance rigs crawl far below highway pace, so brake immediately upon spotting an orange rear triangle.

sec03-R19-card.question_text: What color are the letters printed on a downward-pointing red-and-white yield sign?
sec03-R19-card.teaching_text: Written permit questions frequently test small color details to be sure you distinguish red-lettered yields from white-lettered stops.

sec03-R15-card.question_text: What background and letter colors do destination signs usually use to show directions and distances?
sec03-R15-card.teaching_text: Green panels guide you toward cities and exits while brown panels point toward parks, historic sites, and scenic areas.

sec03-R16-card.question_text: What color combination marks service signs pointing to fuel, rest areas, or hospitals?
sec03-R16-card.teaching_text: Scanning for blue roadside panels helps travelers locate gas, lodging, or emergency medical care without sudden last-second swerves.

sec03-R17-card.question_text: What do the outline form and color of a route-number sign tell a driver?
sec03-R17-card.teaching_text: Recognizing shield styles lets you confirm whether you are on a multi-lane interstate or a local county highway.

sec03-R18-card.question_text: What two-step navigation habit does the New Mexico handbook recommend for reaching unfamiliar destinations?
sec03-R18-card.teaching_text: Checking route numbers before starting out keeps your eyes on traffic instead of hunting street names mid-intersection.

sec03-R20-card.question_text: What two geometric shapes are used for destination guide signs?
sec03-R20-card.teaching_text: Wide rectangular or square boards give highway engineers room to list exit arrows, town names, and mileage clearly.

sec03-R21-card.question_text: What two geometric shapes do motorist service signs use?
sec03-R21-card.teaching_text: Standardized square and rectangular blue boards neatly frame hospital, gas, food, and rest-area icons along highway exits.

sec03-R22-card.question_text: Which five road systems do route-number signs distinguish from one another?
sec03-R22-card.teaching_text: Knowing all five route tiers prevents confusion when identically numbered state and federal highways cross the same town.

sec07-F01-card.question_text: Who is required to obey applicable speed limits on New Mexico roadways?
sec07-F01-card.teaching_text: Shared speed ceilings keep closing speeds predictable so one speeding driver cannot overwhelm everyone else's reaction window.

sec07-F02-card.question_text: How does your travel speed relate to your ability to control the vehicle?
sec07-F02-card.teaching_text: Every extra burst of pace magnifies steering drift and braking demands when a surprise appears ahead.

sec07-F03-card.question_text: What maximum speed does the New Mexico handbook list for a school zone with a posted limit?
sec07-F03-card.teaching_text: Low school-zone speeds give you the short stopping distance needed when children dart out between buses and crosswalks.

sec07-F04-card.question_text: Unless signs post another limit, what is the maximum speed in a New Mexico business or residential area?
sec07-F04-card.teaching_text: Driveways, parked cars, and frequent intersections pack urban blocks with side conflicts that higher speeds cannot handle.

sec07-F05-card.question_text: What default maximum speed applies on New Mexico public highways when no other limit is posted?
sec07-F05-card.teaching_text: Permit tests love pairing unposted public highways against higher rural interstate limits to catch hasty guesses.

sec07-F06-card.question_text: Unless signs state otherwise, what maximum speed does the handbook give for New Mexico rural interstates?
sec07-F06-card.teaching_text: Controlled-access rural interstates remove cross-street traffic, though you still must drop pace whenever signs or weather demand.

sec07-F07-card.question_text: How must you treat a posted minimum speed sign?
sec07-F07-card.teaching_text: Creeping far below freeway speed turns your rear bumper into a rolling wall for fast-approaching traffic.

sec07-F08-card.question_text: What rule governs how slowly you may drive when no minimum speed sign is posted?
sec07-F08-card.teaching_text: Even without a minimum sign, crawling along a clear road forces risky passing maneuvers behind you.

sec07-F09-card.question_text: Which three factors require you to adjust your speed below normal limits?
sec07-F09-card.teaching_text: A posted number only fits ideal conditions, not slick pavement, a heavy load, or an unfolding hazard ahead.

sec07-R28-card.question_text: Which side of the road should you use when traveling slower than surrounding traffic?
sec07-R28-card.teaching_text: Camping in left lanes at a slower pace frustrates following drivers and triggers dangerous right-side passing.

sec07-F10-card.question_text: Who bears responsibility for making sure a parked vehicle creates zero hazard?
sec07-F10-card.teaching_text: Walking away from a poorly placed car still leaves you accountable if it blocks sightlines or rolls.

sec07-F11-card.question_text: How far from moving lanes must you position a parked vehicle?
sec07-F11-card.teaching_text: Leaving a fender or mirror jutting near an active lane invites sideswipes from passing trucks and distracted commuters.

sec07-F12-card.question_text: From which directions should approaching drivers be able to see your parked vehicle?
sec07-F12-card.teaching_text: Tucking a stopped car right behind a blind crest or curve surprises oncoming drivers with zero braking room.

sec07-F13-card.question_text: What kind of location should you choose for parking whenever one is available?
sec07-F13-card.teaching_text: Marked stalls and lots keep stationary cars completely separated from high-speed travel shoulders.

sec07-F14-card.question_text: When should you set the parking brake?
sec07-F14-card.teaching_text: Relying on transmission gears alone can let a parked car creep or roll if bumped or parked on a slight grade.

sec07-F15-card.question_text: How should you leave the transmission when parking a manual-shift vehicle?
sec07-F15-card.teaching_text: Leaving a stick-shift in neutral removes mechanical engine resistance if the parking brake cable ever slackens.

sec07-F16-card.question_text: Where must the gear selector sit when you leave a parked automatic-transmission vehicle?
sec07-F16-card.teaching_text: Stepping out while the selector rests in Drive or Neutral lets the car roll away unattended.

sec07-F17-card.question_text: What must you check right before swinging open a parked vehicle door?
sec07-F17-card.teaching_text: Flinging a door into a bike lane or travel lane gives cyclists and passing cars zero chance to swerve.

sec07-F18-card.question_text: Which side of a parked vehicle should you exit from whenever possible?
sec07-F18-card.teaching_text: Stepping directly onto the sidewalk keeps your body and open door completely out of passing traffic.

sec07-F19-card.question_text: What precaution is required when you have no choice except exiting on the street side?
sec07-F19-card.teaching_text: Timing your exit for a clean gap keeps passing mirrors and bumpers safely away from you.

sec07-F20-card.question_text: How quickly should you shut your vehicle door once you get out?
sec07-F20-card.teaching_text: Standing in the lane with an open door exposes both you and the door panel to passing traffic.

sec07-F21-card.question_text: What rule applies to ignition keys when leaving a parked vehicle?
sec07-F21-card.teaching_text: Keys left in the cabin invite vehicle theft and joyriding crashes within seconds of walking away.

sec07-F22-card.question_text: What final security step does the handbook recommend whenever you leave your vehicle?
sec07-F22-card.teaching_text: Locking up deters opportunistic theft and keeps curious children from climbing inside an unattended car.

sec07-F23-card.question_text: Where should you position your vehicle if parking on a roadway cannot be avoided?
sec07-F23-card.teaching_text: Maximizing lateral buffer space reduces the chance a drifted tire clips your stopped car.

sec07-F24-card.question_text: How should you position your car when you must park along a curbed roadway?
sec07-F24-card.teaching_text: Tucking tight to the curb keeps the travel lane wide enough for buses, trucks, and bikes to pass cleanly.

sec07-F25-card.question_text: How does the New Mexico handbook instruct you to angle your wheels when parking on a hill?
sec07-F25-card.teaching_text: Aiming front tires sharply toward the curb or road edge keeps a rolling car from drifting into center traffic.

sec07-R01-card.question_text: Is parking inside an intersection ever allowed?
sec07-R01-card.teaching_text: A stationary vehicle inside crossing lanes blinds every approach and forces dangerous swerves.

sec07-R02-card.question_text: What parking rule applies to crosswalks and sidewalks?
sec07-R02-card.teaching_text: Blocking marked crossings or walkways forces pedestrians and wheelchair users out into active vehicle lanes.

sec07-R03-card.question_text: When is parking in a construction zone prohibited?
sec07-R03-card.teaching_text: Narrowed cone lanes leave zero room to squeeze past a parked car without endangering road crews.

sec07-R04-card.question_text: Within how many feet of a stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal is parking prohibited?
sec07-R04-card.teaching_text: Parking too close to intersection signs hides critical controls behind your roofline from approaching drivers.

sec07-R05-card.question_text: How many feet must you stay clear when parking near an intersection crosswalk?
sec07-R05-card.teaching_text: Exam questions pit twenty-five feet at crosswalks against thirty feet at signs, and that gap keeps walkers visible.

sec07-R06-card.question_text: At least how many feet from a fire hydrant must a parked vehicle remain?
sec07-R06-card.teaching_text: Firefighters need immediate curb space to connect stiff, high-pressure supply hoses without a car blocking access.

sec07-R07-card.question_text: Parking is prohibited within how many feet of a railroad crossing?
sec07-R07-card.teaching_text: Cars parked near tracks block sightlines down the rails and hide flashing crossing signals.

sec07-R08-card.question_text: What is the maximum distance your parked tires may sit away from the curb?
sec07-R08-card.teaching_text: Parking wider than eighteen inches leaves the outer side of your car jutting into the travel lane.

sec07-R09-card.question_text: What same-side curb buffer must you keep clear beside a firehouse driveway?
sec07-R09-card.teaching_text: Heavy fire engines need a wide turning radius right out of the bay doors when an alarm sounds.

sec07-R10-card.question_text: What opposite-curb distance is off-limits for parking across from a firehouse driveway?
sec07-R10-card.teaching_text: Long ladder trucks swing wide across the far curb when turning out, making seventy-five feet a classic test number.

sec07-R11-card.question_text: Which access openings and curb features must you never block when parking?
sec07-R11-card.teaching_text: Blocking alleys, private roads, driveways, or sidewalk curb cuts traps property owners and wheelchair users alike.

sec07-R12-card.question_text: Is parking allowed on bridges, overpasses, tunnels, or underpasses?
sec07-R12-card.teaching_text: Elevated decks and enclosed tunnels lack escape shoulders, turning any stopped car into an instant bottleneck.

sec07-R13-card.question_text: May you park facing against traffic on the wrong side of a street?
sec07-R13-card.teaching_text: Pulling across oncoming lanes to enter and exit a left-curb spot sets up head-on collisions.

sec07-R14-card.question_text: What authorization is required to park in a marked disability space?
sec07-R14-card.teaching_text: Accessible stalls provide essential ramp and transfer room that unauthorized cars must never occupy.

sec07-R15-card.question_text: May you stop or park on the street side beside a car already parked at the curb?
sec07-R15-card.teaching_text: Double-parking traps the curb car inside and forces moving traffic to swerve across center lines.

sec07-R16-card.question_text: What is the rule on parking directly on railroad tracks?
sec07-R16-card.teaching_text: Trains can arrive at high speed on any active rail before an unattended vehicle could ever be moved.

sec07-R17-card.question_text: What must you do wherever a posted sign prohibits parking?
sec07-R17-card.teaching_text: Posted bans protect hidden sightlines, bus stops, and emergency turnouts even when the curb looks open.

sec07-R18-card.question_text: What does a white-painted curb allow?
sec07-R18-card.teaching_text: White zones keep passenger drop-offs moving quickly instead of letting long-term parkers clog entrances.

sec07-R19-card.question_text: What restriction does a yellow-painted curb mark?
sec07-R19-card.teaching_text: Checking nearby curb lettering or signs tells you whether freight loading or time caps apply.

sec07-R20-card.question_text: What does a red-painted curb signify, and may you stand or park there?
sec07-R20-card.teaching_text: Even idling inside your car at a red curb blocks fire apparatus when seconds count.

sec07-R21-card.question_text: Who is a blue-painted curb reserved for?
sec07-R21-card.teaching_text: Blue curb markings pair with accessible signage so drivers never accidentally take reserved mobility space.

sec07-R22-card.question_text: How do common traffic violations affect your driving record under the point system?
sec07-R22-card.teaching_text: More dangerous moving violations stack steeper point totals so repeat risk-takers lose driving privileges faster.

sec07-R23-card.question_text: How many points in twelve months trigger a license suspension, and how long does that suspension last?
sec07-R23-card.teaching_text: Hitting twelve points inside one year sidelines your license for twelve straight months, a classic MVD test benchmark.

sec07-R24-card.question_text: Where can you get the list of point-bearing traffic offenses in New Mexico?
sec07-R24-card.teaching_text: Checking the official MVD point schedule shows exactly how fast speeding or careless citations add up.

sec07-R25-card.question_text: Instead of adding traffic points, what does driving without insurance require?
sec07-R25-card.teaching_text: Exam writers love testing that lacking insurance skips the point chart and sends you straight before a judge.

sec07-R26-card.question_text: What happens instead of traffic points if you drive without vehicle registration?
sec07-R26-card.teaching_text: Just like missing insurance, expired or missing registration triggers a mandatory court date rather than driver points.

sec07-R27-card.question_text: What penalties can follow a court appearance for driving without insurance or registration?
sec07-R27-card.teaching_text: Skipping points does not mean getting off lightly when a judge can impose extra fines or suspend your license.

sec09-F01-card.question_text: When should you use high-beam headlights, and what separate conditions restrict them?
sec09-F01-card.teaching_text: Bright beams maximize open-road sight distance, provided nobody is oncoming, close ahead, or packed into heavy traffic.

sec09-F02-card.question_text: How much farther do high beams let you see compared with low beams according to the handbook?
sec09-F02-card.teaching_text: Doubling your illuminated sightline gives critical extra seconds to brake for dark hazards on unlit highways.

sec09-F03-card.question_text: In which three roadway settings is high-beam visibility especially helpful?
sec09-F03-card.teaching_text: Extra reach spots unlit curve markers, cones, and pedestrians walking dark shoulders before you overrun them.

sec09-F04-card.question_text: At roughly what distance must you dim your high beams for an approaching vehicle?
sec09-F04-card.teaching_text: New Mexico expresses oncoming dimming as roughly one block so you drop glare before blinding the opposing driver.

sec09-F05-card.question_text: Within what following distance, or in what traffic condition, must you switch to low beams?
sec09-F05-card.teaching_text: High beams within two hundred feet or in heavy traffic bounce blinding glare off the lead driver's mirrors.

sec09-F06-card.question_text: Why must you choose low beams instead of high beams in fog, heavy snow, or heavy rain?
sec09-F06-card.teaching_text: High-angled brights bounce straight back off water droplets and snowflakes, turning the windshield into a white wall.

sec09-F07-card.question_text: What auxiliary lights should you add, if equipped, during fog, heavy snow, or heavy rain?
sec09-F07-card.teaching_text: Low-mounted fog lamps throw a wide beam underneath suspended mist without reflecting glare back into your eyes.

sec09-F08-card.question_text: May you drive using parking lamps alone instead of full headlights?
sec09-F08-card.teaching_text: Dim marker bulbs exist only to outline a stationary car and fail to light the lane or make moving speed clear.

sec09-F09-card.question_text: What rule of thumb triggers turning on your headlights whenever other road users become hard to see?
sec09-F09-card.teaching_text: Switching headlights on in dim conditions makes your approaching car stand out just as much as it lights the road.

sec09-F10-card.question_text: What lighting step must accompany turning on your windshield wipers?
sec09-F10-card.teaching_text: Rain spray and overcast skies camouflage gray and silver cars unless full headlights and taillights are glowing.

sec09-F11-card.question_text: When should you switch on headlights at dusk instead of waiting for pitch darkness?
sec09-F11-card.teaching_text: Twilight flattens road contrast while drivers' eyes are still adjusting, hiding unlit vehicles in long shadows.

sec09-F12-card.question_text: Why should you turn on headlights when driving away from a rising or setting sun?
sec09-F12-card.teaching_text: Oncoming drivers staring straight into a low horizon sun only see dark silhouettes unless your headlights pierce the glare.

sec09-F13-card.question_text: How can you use your headlights briefly to alert another road user to your presence?
sec09-F13-card.teaching_text: A quick beam flash catches attention silently across intersections or glass cabins where a light horn tap might go unheard.

sec09-F14-card.question_text: When should you use your horn, and what touch fits when danger is not immediate?
sec09-F14-card.teaching_text: A polite tap communicates awareness calmly without startling someone into swerving or freezing.

sec09-F15-card.question_text: How should you warn a pedestrian or cyclist who looks about to move into your lane?
sec09-F15-card.teaching_text: Blasting a loud horn right beside an exposed rider can make them wobble straight into your path.

sec09-F16-card.question_text: What horn signal helps if a driver starts drifting toward your lane while you overtake them?
sec09-F16-card.teaching_text: A quick tap snaps a lane-changer's attention to their blind spot before fenders touch.

sec09-F17-card.question_text: How should you alert an inattentive driver who might not notice your vehicle?
sec09-F17-card.teaching_text: Getting noticed early prevents a distracted driver from pulling out right across your bow.

sec09-F18-card.question_text: At which three zero-visibility features does the handbook suggest giving a light horn tap?
sec09-F18-card.teaching_text: Sound travels over crests, around tight rock corners, and past alley walls before bumpers can see each other.

sec09-F19-card.question_text: What kind of horn signal is called for when a child or older person is about to step into danger?
sec09-F19-card.teaching_text: Immediate danger demands an unmistakable sharp blast that freezes someone before they step in front of moving tires.

sec09-F20-card.question_text: Which horn signal should you use when another vehicle is on the verge of hitting you?
sec09-F20-card.teaching_text: A forceful blast cuts through cabin music and road noise fast enough to trigger emergency braking or steering.

sec09-F21-card.question_text: What horn action should you take if your own out-of-control vehicle is sliding toward someone?
sec09-F21-card.teaching_text: When brakes or tires cannot stop your slide, a loud blast gives bystanders a fighting chance to jump clear.

sec09-F22-card.question_text: Which four maneuvers always require using your turn signal beforehand?
sec09-F22-card.teaching_text: Every lateral shift changes lane occupancy, so signaling lets surrounding traffic anticipate your path.

sec09-F23-card.question_text: Should you still signal a change of direction when no other road user appears to be around?
sec09-F23-card.teaching_text: The motorcycle or pedestrian you failed to spot is the exact person who needs your blinker most.

sec09-F24-card.question_text: At least how many feet before turning must you start your turn signal in New Mexico?
sec09-F24-card.teaching_text: Flicking the lever mid-turn warns nobody, whereas one hundred feet gives following drivers real reaction space.

sec09-F25-card.question_text: When should you delay turning on your signal if another car waits at a driveway before your actual turn?
sec09-F25-card.teaching_text: Signaling too early tricks a waiting side-driveway driver into thinking you are turning in, causing them to pull out.

sec09-F26-card.question_text: What must you check right after finishing a turn or lane change?
sec09-F26-card.teaching_text: Gentle lane shifts often fail to trip the automatic cancel cam, requiring a manual click off.

sec09-F27-card.question_text: Which vehicle lights notify following drivers that you are slowing down?
sec09-F27-card.teaching_text: Glowing red brake lamps bridge the reaction gap before a following driver notices your bumper getting closer.

sec09-F28-card.question_text: How should you time your slowdown, and what should you do before an unavoidable sudden stop if time permits?
sec09-F28-card.teaching_text: Braking early flashes your taillights in time to keep a tailgating car out of your trunk.

sec09-R13-card.question_text: Why is it essential to warn other drivers before changing direction or slowing?
sec09-R13-card.teaching_text: Drivers around you need a couple of seconds to perceive a blinker or brake light and adjust pace safely.

sec09-R14-card.question_text: What dangerous misunderstanding can a turn signal left blinking after a maneuver cause?
sec09-R14-card.teaching_text: Cross-street drivers may pull right across your bumper believing your leftover blinker means you are turning off.

sec09-R01-card.question_text: What visibility goal comes first if your vehicle breaks down along a highway?
sec09-R01-card.teaching_text: High-speed traffic assumes roadside silhouettes are moving unless bright visual warnings announce a stationary hazard.

sec09-R02-card.question_text: Which communication tools should you use, if available, to report your own or someone else's breakdown?
sec09-R02-card.teaching_text: Alerting highway authorities brings patrol protection and tow clearance before a roadside stall causes a crash.

sec09-R03-card.question_text: What two contact details may roadside emergency signs post for stranded motorists?
sec09-R03-card.teaching_text: Remote New Mexico stretches post dedicated help numbers and radio channels so drivers reach dispatch fast.

sec09-R04-card.question_text: Where should you move your vehicle if mechanical trouble forces a stop?
sec09-R04-card.teaching_text: Coasting completely off the travel surface while you still have momentum prevents a live-lane collision.

sec09-R05-card.question_text: Which lights must you switch on to signal vehicle trouble?
sec09-R05-card.teaching_text: Flashing hazard lamps instantly tell approaching drivers your car is disabled or crawling, not cruising normally.

sec09-R06-card.question_text: If mechanical trouble traps your car on the roadway, where should you try to stop and which blind spots must you avoid?
sec09-R06-card.teaching_text: Stopping just beyond a hilltop or blind bend hides your stalled bumper until fast traffic crests right onto you.

sec09-R07-card.question_text: Why does the manual advise placing warning flares behind a disabled vehicle?
sec09-R07-card.teaching_text: Advance roadside markers alert fast highway packs early enough to merge cleanly away from your shoulder.

sec09-R08-card.question_text: Where must you keep yourself during a breakdown, and what repair action is forbidden inside a traffic lane?
sec09-R08-card.teaching_text: Crouching beside a jacked car inside an active travel lane puts your body inches from highway bumpers.

sec09-R09-card.question_text: Which position relative to another vehicle should you avoid cruising in?
sec09-R09-card.teaching_text: Riding slightly behind and beside another car hides you right where an unexpected lane change will clip you.

sec09-R10-card.question_text: How should you adjust your spacing relative to an adjacent car so its driver can spot you easily?
sec09-R10-card.teaching_text: Shifting slightly forward or rearward puts your headlights cleanly into the other driver's peripheral view or mirrors.

sec09-R11-card.question_text: How should you manage time spent in another driver's blind spot while passing?
sec09-R11-card.teaching_text: Completing a pass promptly minimizes the window where the overtaken driver might drift over unaware.

sec09-R12-card.question_text: Why must you avoid cruising alongside a bus or large truck?
sec09-R12-card.teaching_text: Commercial rigs have massive side No-Zones where an entire sedan vanishes from the cab mirrors.

sec14-F01-card.question_text: What routine schedule helps lower the risk of a sudden mechanical failure while driving?
sec14-F01-card.teaching_text: Scheduled fluid, belt, and brake inspections catch worn parts before they fail on rural highways.

sec14-F02-card.question_text: What is the very first action the New Mexico manual directs if your regular brakes quit working?
sec14-F02-card.teaching_text: Rapid pumping can build enough backup hydraulic pressure in a failing line to slow the vehicle down.

sec14-F03-card.question_text: If pumping fails to restore brake pressure, how should you operate the parking-brake handle?
sec14-F03-card.teaching_text: Yanking the emergency brake violently locks rear tires and throws the vehicle into an uncontrolled spin.

sec14-F04-card.question_text: What must you stay ready to do if applying the parking brake triggers a rear-wheel skid?
sec14-F04-card.teaching_text: Letting off cable tension right away restores rolling tire grip before the back end whips sideways.

sec14-F05-card.question_text: If both pumping and the parking brake fail to stop you, what transmission and steering steps come next?
sec14-F05-card.teaching_text: Dropping into lower gears uses engine drag to scrub speed while you guide onto a safe shoulder.

sec14-F06-card.question_text: Once stopped, may you slowly drive a vehicle that has lost working brakes to a repair shop?
sec14-F06-card.teaching_text: Rolling even one block without reliable stopping power endangers every intersection and pedestrian ahead.

sec14-F07-card.question_text: How should you hold and aim the steering wheel right when a tire suddenly deflates or blows out?
sec14-F07-card.teaching_text: A blown tire yanks hard toward the flat side, requiring two-handed control to stay inside your lane.

sec14-F08-card.question_text: How does the New Mexico manual instruct you to shed speed during a tire blowout?
sec14-F08-card.teaching_text: Stomping the brake pedal pitches heavy nose weight onto the shredded rim and triggers a spin.

sec14-F09-card.question_text: Where should you come to a stop after slowing down from a tire blowout?
sec14-F09-card.teaching_text: Stopping inside a live travel lane leaves you exposed to distracted highway traffic coming from behind.

sec14-F10-card.question_text: What happens to steering effort if your engine dies while moving, and how should you react?
sec14-F10-card.teaching_text: Losing power-steering assist stiffens the wheel dramatically without locking mechanical front-tire steering.

sec14-F11-card.question_text: Where should you steer after an engine stall, and how does brake pedal effort change?
sec14-F11-card.teaching_text: Depleted vacuum power assist means stopping safely on the shoulder takes noticeably firmer leg force.

sec14-F12-card.question_text: What should you try first if your headlights abruptly cut out at night?
sec14-F12-card.teaching_text: Flipping a loose contact or tripped breaker can restore forward beams immediately without losing sightlines.

sec14-F13-card.question_text: Which three other lighting controls can help if toggling the main switch fails to bring dead headlights back?
sec14-F13-card.teaching_text: Auxiliary bulbs cast faint curbside glow while alerting other motorists where your dark car is moving.

sec14-F14-card.question_text: Where must you take your vehicle immediately if failed headlights stay dark?
sec14-F14-card.teaching_text: Continuing down unlit pavement outruns visibility and leaves oncoming cars blind to your lane.

sec14-F15-card.question_text: What is your immediate gear and visual response if a sticking accelerator keeps revving higher?
sec14-F15-card.teaching_text: Shifting to neutral severs engine torque from the wheels instantly while keeping power steering alive.

sec14-F16-card.question_text: In what exact order do you leave traffic and shut off a revving engine after selecting neutral?
sec14-F16-card.teaching_text: Killing ignition before stopping steals power assist and risks locking the steering wheel in traffic.

sec14-R01-card.question_text: Which three emergency actions does the manual list as possible ways to avoid an impending crash?
sec14-R01-card.teaching_text: Remembering steering and throttle options alongside braking opens escape paths when stopping room runs short.

sec14-R02-card.question_text: Where should you look to confirm how your specific car's antilock braking system operates?
sec14-R02-card.teaching_text: Checking brake design before emergencies strike prevents pumping an antilock pedal by mistake.

sec14-R03-card.question_text: How should you press the brake pedal for a maximum emergency stop with working ABS?
sec14-R03-card.teaching_text: Firm continuous pressure lets computer-controlled valves modulate wheel grip far faster than human feet.

sec14-R04-card.question_text: How should you respond if the brake pedal vibrates or pushes back during an ABS panic stop?
sec14-R04-card.teaching_text: Lifting your foot when the pedal pulses shuts off emergency braking right when you need maximum stopping.

sec14-R05-card.question_text: How hard should you apply the brakes during an emergency stop in a vehicle without ABS?
sec14-R05-card.teaching_text: Threshold braking keeps tires rolling for maximum pavement friction and steering control.

sec14-R06-card.question_text: What immediate pedal move unlocks skidding tires in a car without ABS?
sec14-R06-card.teaching_text: Letting off pressure frees sliding rubber to roll freely again so front wheels regain steering bite.

sec14-R07-card.question_text: Once releasing the pedal stops a non-ABS skid, how do you finish bringing the vehicle to a halt?
sec14-R07-card.teaching_text: Controlled squeeze-and-release cycles shed remaining speed without sliding helplessly into the hazard.

sec14-R08-card.question_text: Why does the handbook suggest considering an evasive turn when an obstacle appears close ahead?
sec14-R08-card.teaching_text: At highway speed, steering clear by one lane width takes far less distance than braking to zero.

sec14-R09-card.question_text: How should you grip the wheel during an emergency swerve, and what follows the initial dodge?
sec14-R09-card.teaching_text: Balanced two-handed steering stops violent body roll from flinging you into a secondary crash.

sec14-R10-card.question_text: Where should your steering aim during an emergency maneuver?
sec14-R10-card.teaching_text: Staring straight at a tree or stalled bumper pulls your hands toward the exact object you want to miss.

sec14-R11-card.question_text: What combined maneuver does ABS make possible without skidding during an emergency?
sec14-R11-card.teaching_text: Keeping front tires rolling under heavy brake pressure lets you scrub speed and dodge simultaneously.

sec14-R12-card.question_text: What three-step foot-and-hand sequence executes a quick emergency turn without ABS?
sec14-R12-card.teaching_text: Separating hard braking from sharp steering keeps non-ABS front tires from locking straight.

sec14-R13-card.question_text: What happens in a non-ABS quick turn if you lock the front wheels or crank the wheel too sharply?
sec14-R13-card.teaching_text: Overworked or locked front rubber loses lateral bite completely and slides straight into the obstacle.

sec14-R14-card.question_text: Against which impact angles can accelerating save you, and what must exist ahead?
sec14-R14-card.teaching_text: Braking for a red-light runner coming at your door pins you inside the impact point when speeding clear dodges it.

sec14-R15-card.question_text: What must you do once accelerating pulls you clear of an immediate crash threat?
sec14-R15-card.teaching_text: Dropping back to normal pace keeps burst acceleration from creating a new hazard down the block.

sec14-R16-card.question_text: How do rain, snow, or ice combine with high speed during sudden turns or stops?
sec14-R16-card.teaching_text: Reduced surface friction cannot hold abrupt high-speed inputs that dry summer asphalt forgives.

sec14-R17-card.question_text: What happens between your tires and the pavement when a skid begins?
sec14-R17-card.teaching_text: Without rolling friction against asphalt, steering inputs and brake pressure lose normal authority.

sec14-R18-card.question_text: Once a skid is already underway, what does the New Mexico manual warn regarding the brake pedal?
sec14-R18-card.teaching_text: Touching the brakes during a slide locks remaining tire rotation and deepens loss of control.
